“KILDARE COMMUTERS ARE BEING BADLY LET DOWN” – COUNCILLOR BILL CLEAR DEMANDS URGENT ACTION ON RAIL OVERCROWDING

Councillor Bill Clear, Mayor of Naas and Independent Ireland representative, has called on the Government and Irish Rail to take immediate action to address severe overcrowding on commuter trains serving Sallins, Naas, Newbridge and the wider Kildare area.

Speaking from Sallins Train Station this morning, Councillor Clear expressed his frustration at the continued delays to DART+ South West and the lack of additional train capacity for Kildare commuters.

“Every morning, commuters are being forced onto seriously overcrowded trains. Passengers are standing for long journeys, and I have received reports of people fainting due to overcrowding. This is becoming a serious health and safety concern, and something needs to be done urgently.”

Councillor Clear highlighted the introduction of a new morning train service from Adamstown into Dublin, which commenced today.

“I welcome additional rail services, but this new train starts in Adamstown. It provides no additional seats for passengers boarding in Sallins or Newbridge, where overcrowding is already a major problem.

“We are seeing investment and improvements elsewhere on the rail network, while Kildare commuters are being asked to wait.”

The DART+ South West project, which would extend electrified services to Hazelhatch and Celbridge, has been pushed back under the Government's investment programme, with construction currently scheduled for 2030 or later.

“Kildare is one of the fastest-growing counties in Ireland. Thousands of people depend on the railway to get to work and college, yet the infrastructure is simply not keeping pace with population growth.

“I have been in regular contact with Irish Rail demanding additional carriages on existing services. We cannot wait another six or seven years for improvements.”

Councillor Clear confirmed that he is asking the Independent Ireland party leadership to raise the matter directly with the Minister for Transport through parliamentary questions.

He is also calling for an urgent review of morning commuter capacity, additional carriages where possible, and a firm commitment that Kildare services will benefit from the redeployment of trains when the new DART fleet enters service in 2027.

“I am also asking commuters to contact Irish Rail and the Department of Transport to make their concerns known.

“Kildare commuters have been patient for long enough. We need more carriages, more capacity and a proper timetable for improvements. The people of Kildare deserve better than this.”

Ulster GAA, the Irish FA and Ulster Rugby recently brought together 24 young sports volunteers for their annual Multi-Sport Youth Forum, providing an opportunity for young people to share their views and help shape the future of safe sport.
The event included a special tour of the Clearer Twist National Stadium at Windsor Park, home of Northern Ireland Football, alongside a comprehensive youth consultation facilitated with Sport NI.
The consultation focused on the important theme of Safe Sport, providing young people with an opportunity to share their experiences, perspectives and ideas on how sporting environments can be made safer, more inclusive and more positive for everyone.
The feedback gathered will help inform wider discussions and contribute to the development of Safe Sport policy, ensuring that the voices and experiences of young people in Ulster are central to shaping the future of sport.
The forum highlighted the commitment of Ulster GAA, the Irish FA and Ulster Rugby to working collaboratively and ensuring young people have a meaningful voice in decisions that affect their participation and experiences in sport.

[스압]미군 쫓아냈다가 피눈물 흘리고 땅 4천 에이커까지 갖다 바친 필리핀 근황.txt (feat. 치외법권 명분 & 韓 안보 현실)

님들아, 최근 아세안 정상회담에서 국내언론이 싹 다 입 닫고 보도 안 하는 개충격적인 뉴스 하나 떴는데 암?

지금 필리핀이 미군 다시 모셔오려고 자국 영토 4,000 에이커를 아예 미국 대사관급 '치외법권' 땅으로 상납해버림 ㅋㅋㅋㅋ

단순히 "그냥 땅 줄게"가 아니라 미국이 어떤 명분을 걸었고, 필리핀이 왜 그걸 넙죽 받았는지, 그리고 우리나라 정치인들 하는 꼬라지가 얼마나 답이 없는지 쭉 훑어보자.

1. 배부른 소리 하다가 미군 쫓아낸 90년대 필리핀

원래 필리핀은 1946년 독립 이후에도 클라크 공군기지, 수빅만 해군기지 등 아시아 최대 규모 미군 기지가 박혀있던 곳임. 그냥 미군 우산 아래서 꿀 빨면서 안보 걱정 1도 없이 살았음.

근데 80년대 말~90년대 초 되니까 필리핀 내부 좌파랑 민족주의자들이 "미군은 점령군이다! 양키 고 홈!" 이러면서 매일 반미 시위하고 난리를 침. 

마침 1991년에 피나투보 화산 폭발까지 터지니까 미국 입장에서도 "어 그래? 꼬우면 뺄게~" 하고 1992년에 미군 병력 싹 다 철수시켜버림.

2. 미군 나가자마자 시작된 중국의 참교육 타임

미군 빠지자마자 제일 신난 게 누구겠음? 

바로 중국(중공)임 ㅋㅋ

그전까지는 미군 무서워서 찍소리도 못 하던 중국이 미군 나가자마자 필리핀 앞바다(남중국해, 팔라완 인근)로 떼거지로 몰려와서 깡패짓 시작함.

필리핀 EEZ(배타적경제수역) 안에 있는 암초에 지들 마음대로 콘크리트 붓고 인공섬 만들어서 군사기지화함.

자체 해·공군력이 열세인 필리핀 해경선이나 어선 지나가면 중국 해경선이 물대포 쏘고 배로 들이받으면서 개무시함.

말 그대로 지들 안방 앞바다 다 뺏기고 수십 년 동안 중국한테 온갖 수모란 수모는 다 당함.

3. '팍스 실리카'라는 명분으로 4,000 에이커 치외법권 상납

발등에 불 떨어진 필리핀 마르코스 주니어 대통령이 "미군 형님들 제발 다시 와주세요" 하고 바이든 때부터 트럼프 행정부까지 피땀 흘리면서 로비함.

이번 아세안 정상회담에서도 필리핀 대통령이 트럼프랑 마코 루비오 국무장관한테 얼마나 깍듯이 대하는지 의전 영상 보면 눈물날 지경임.

근데 땅 4,000 에이커를 그냥 주면 필리핀 국민들도 반발하니까 미국이랑 필리핀이 내세운 공식 명분이 기가 막힘.

명분:
 미국의 글로벌 공급망 프로젝트 '팍스 실리카(Pax Silica)' 유치중국이 희토류랑 핵심 광물 가지고 자원 무기화하고 장난질 치니까, 트럼프가 탈중국 첨단 공급망 동맹인 '팍스 실리카'를 띄움. 

그 일환으로 필리핀 뉴클락 시티 일대에 희토류 가공 및 AI·첨단 제조업 공업 단지를 짓겠다는 명분을 내세운 거임.

치외법권을 요구한 명분: 
"중국 공산당 간첩 원천 차단"트럼프가 "중국 공산당 빨갱이 간첩들이 전 세계 돌아다니면서 기술 도둑질하고 첩보질하는 게 너무 심하다. 

그러니 이 4,000 에이커 첨단 제조 단지는 미국 대사관과 똑같은 치외법권 지역으로 인정해 줘. 

그래야 미군이나 미 해병대가 직접 들어가서 지키고 중국 간첩들 얼씬도 못 하게 막지"라고 딜을 건 거임.

필리핀?

 "경제 발전 + 첨단 산업 유치 + 미군 주둔 명분 확보"까지 일석삼조라고 판단하고 뒤도 안 돌아보고 바로 OK 사인함 ㅋㅋㅋ

필리핀 내부 좌빨들이

"공장 부지가 무슨 대사관이냐! 주권 침해다!" 하고 시위하는데도 대통령이 씹고 그냥 미국에 갖다 바침. 

한 번 쫓아낸 미군 다시 불러들이려고 '첨단 산업 단지'라는 명분 아래 자국 영토 치외법권까지 내어주면서, 32년 만에 미군 기지 9개 다시 세우고 F-16 최신형 사 오면서 대만·중국 코앞 상륙훈련까지 뛰고 있음.

4. 결론: 남의 나라 피눈물 보고도 정신 못 차리는 한국

필리핀은 이미 쫓아낸 미군 다시 모셔오려고 자존심 다 버리고 '팍스 실리카' 명분까지 엮어가며 땅 4천 에이커를 치외법권으로 갖다 바치고 있는데, 

대한민국 꼬라지 보셈 ㅋㅋ

6.25 때 미군 3만 7천 명 죽고 20만 명 팔다리 잘려가며 지켜준 나라에서, 요즘 정치권이랑 여론 보면 아직도 '안미경중' 이딴 소리하면서 양다리 걸치고 있음.

필리핀 국방장관이나 대통령은 대놓고 중국 욕하면서 들이받는데, 한국 정치인들은 중국 간첩단 설치고 서해 공정 쳐도 찍소리도 못 하고 눈치 보기 바쁨.

심지어 남들은 땅까지 주면서 모셔 오려는 미군이 이미 한국에 주둔해 있는데도, 방위비 분담금 핑계 대고 주한미군 철수니 뭐니 하면서 있는 미군마저 흔들어 대고 있음.

요약:

필리핀이 반미 시위하다 1992년에 미군 내쫓고 30년간 중국한테 앞바다 뺏기며 온갖 수모 다 당함.

정신 차린 필리핀이 미군 다시 부르려고 'AI·희토류 첨단 제조 단지(팍스 실리카) 유치 및 중국 간첩 차단'이라는 명분을 내세워 자국 땅 4천 에이커를 대사관급 치외법권으로 미국에 상납함.

한국은 이미  있는 귀한 주한미군도 못 지켜서 안달 난 행태를 반복 중임.

역사에서 배우지 못하는 민족은 미래가 없다는데, 30년 전 필리핀 테크트리 그대로 타려는 거 보면 진짜 소름 돋는다.

How the Philippines Went From Kicking Out the U.S. Military to Offering 4,000 Acres of Extraterritorial Land Under "Pax Silica" (And What It Means for South Korea)

A commentary from the Korean-language geopolitics channel Michael Sim (MS) TV highlights an underreported angle from the 2026 ASEAN Summit in Manila: the dramatic turnaround in Philippine foreign policy toward the United States, framed as a stark contrast to South Korea's current diplomatic posture.

While commentators and historians hold differing views on the long-term implications of foreign military basing and industrial sovereignty, the trajectory of the Philippines over the past three decades offers a notable case study in regional security.

1. The 1992 U.S. Withdrawal and Its Aftermath

Following its independence in 1946, the Philippines hosted major U.S. installations—most notably Clark Air Base and Subic Bay Naval Base—which served as pillars of American power projection in the Indo-Pacific.

The Push for Withdrawal: By the late 1980s and early 1990s, growing anti-base sentiment, nationalist movements, and domestic political opposition framed the U.S. presence as a remnant of colonialism. Combined with the 1991 eruption of Mount Pinatubo, which heavily damaged Clark Air Base, the Philippine Senate voted against extending the base leases, leading to a full U.S. withdrawal in 1992.

The Security Vacuum: According to the commentary, the absence of a permanent U.S. deterrent left the Philippines vulnerable in the South China Sea. Beginning in the mid-1990s (such as the 1995 Mischief Reef incident) and accelerating in recent years around Scarborough Shoal and Palawan, China expanded its maritime footprint—building artificial islands within the Philippines' Exclusive Economic Zone (EEZ) and frequently clashing with Philippine Coast Guard vessels and fishing boats using water cannons and blocking maneuvers.
2. Reversing Course: Lobbying and the "Pax Silica" Justification

Under President Ferdinand Marcos Jr., Manila has actively sought to rebuild its security alliance with Washington, expanding access to nine military sites under the Enhanced Defense Cooperation Agreement (EDCA), acquiring upgraded F-16 fighter jets, and conducting large-scale joint amphibious exercises with U.S. Marines.

To secure deeper U.S. commitment without triggering immediate domestic backlash over pure military basing, Michael Sim (MS) TV points to a specific economic and security rationale used by Washington and Manila:

The Official Premise ("Pax Silica"): Framed around countering China's dominance over rare earth elements and critical supply chains, the U.S. introduced the "Pax Silica" initiative—an effort to build non-Chinese AI, semiconductor, and critical mineral processing hubs. Under this framework, the Philippines agreed to allocate roughly 4,000 acres in the New Clark City area (Tarlac) for an advanced AI and rare-earth manufacturing complex.

The Extraterritoriality Clause: The commentary notes that the U.S. requested—and Manila agreed to—granting this 4,000-acre industrial zone extraterritorial status equivalent to a U.S. embassy. The stated justification was to prevent Chinese espionage and intellectual property theft, effectively allowing U.S. security forces or Marines to guard the perimeter directly. While domestic Marxist and anti-imperialist groups protested the deal as an infringement on sovereignty, the Marcos administration prioritized strategic alignment and industrial investment.
3. The Debate Over South Korea's Strategic Posture

In the video, the host contrasts Manila’s assertive outreach toward Washington and vocal criticism of Beijing with South Korea’s foreign policy debates:

The Critique of "Strategic Ambiguity": Critics aligned with this viewpoint argue that South Korea—despite its alliance forged during the Korean War and decades of U.S. security guarantees—often hesitates to take a firm stance against Beijing due to economic interdependence (a posture often referred to as Anmi-Gyeongjung, or "security with the U.S., economy with China"). From this perspective, domestic friction over defense cost-sharing or U.S. troop presence risks repeating the Philippines' 1992 miscalculation.

Counter-Perspectives in Seoul: Conversely, proponents of a more balanced or cautious approach in South Korea argue that Seoul's geopolitical reality differs significantly from Manila's. Because South Korea shares close geographic proximity with China, relies heavily on Chinese trade for its export-driven economy, and requires Beijing's leverage regarding North Korea's nuclear program, many South Korean policymakers emphasize careful diplomatic hedging rather than overt confrontation.
TL;DR:

1992: Domestic opposition and a volcanic eruption led to the U.S. military leaving the Philippines, which critics argue created a vacuum that enabled decades of Chinese maritime pressure in the South China Sea.

2026: As highlighted by Michael Sim (MS) TV, Manila has pivoted back toward Washington—not only expanding U.S. base access, but also offering 4,000 acres in New Clark City with embassy-level extraterritorial status under the "Pax Silica" AI and rare-earth supply chain initiative to deter Chinese espionage.

The Takeaway: Geopolitical commentators point to the Philippines as a cautionary tale for allies like South Korea, sparking ongoing debate over how middle powers should balance economic ties with China against formal security alliances with the United States.

text:
Podcast Summary | Armchair Expert with Dax Shepard: Rena Malik (on sexual health)

Overview
Sexual health is presented as a window into overall health, and the failure to treat it seriously is framed as a missed opportunity for both patients and clinicians. Rena Malik, a urologist and surgeon, argues that sexual function reflects vascular, neurological, hormonal, and psychological systems, and that untreated sexual problems can drive depression, anxiety, and reduced productivity. Her central claim is that technical success in medicine is meaningless if patients do not understand how treatment will change their lives, and that shame and unrealistic information keep people from seeking help for years. She makes the case for faster health literacy through public education, for harm reduction over dismissal when patients raise concerns like penis size, and for treating sex as a marker of health that deserves curiosity rather than avoidance.

Key Themes
- Surgical success is incomplete without patient understanding: a technically successful operation can still fail if the patient never learns how their body and daily life will change afterward.
- Sexual dysfunction is often an early signal of broader health risk, including heart attacks, strokes, and dementia, so dismissing it misses a chance to catch serious disease.
- Shame and lack of realistic information about normal function keep people from seeking help, often for five to ten years, which pushes them toward snake oil or dangerous fixes.
- Clinical questions about sex are insufficient; asking why someone is or is not having sex reveals treatable issues like pain, arousal difficulty, or lost desire.
- Constant stress blocks arousal because it activates the fight-or-flight system, while arousal requires the parasympathetic system and presence.
- Cardiovascular exercise produces erectile function improvements comparable in magnitude to Viagra, and strength training supports hormones, muscle mass, and libido.
- The pelvic floor is central to sex and orgasm, and pelvic floor dysfunction is underdiagnosed, with hypertonic muscles causing pain, urgency, and erection problems.
- Pornography is best framed like alcohol: frequency, context, and coping use matter more than the substance itself, and moral incongruence often makes use worse.
- Penis size is a status signal generated within male peer groups, not a measure of skill or partner pleasure, and it is largely unrelated to a partner's experience.

Detailed Summary

The guest grew up in a conservative Indian immigrant household where sex was never discussed. The only message she received was to avoid boys because boys only wanted sex. Her parents arrived in Buffalo, New York, in 1975 and were among the first four Indian families there, after missing a train to Albany because they misunderstood the pronunciation; a friend suggested Buffalo, where her mother found a nursing job. Her father taught math for a time before becoming a real estate agent. Their marriage was a love marriage, considered taboo in India at the time, and they met on a train when her father asked her mother to buy his ticket and get drinks, then flirted and asked her to a movie. She gave a fake name and claimed to be a doctor at Rohtak Medical College, did not show up, and he later searched the college floor by floor until they bumped into each other on a staircase.

She did not initially want to be a surgeon, but a rotation changed her mind because she liked the tangible, immediate work of fixing something rather than only managing disease. She chose urology after observing that urologists were smart but calm and were on the cusp of robotic surgery at the time. She explored ENT and ophthalmology before deciding urologists were her people, and a resident friend invited her into a robotic kidney surgery that she found the coolest surgery she had seen.

Her comfort discussing sensitive topics came from deciding to treat genitals as just another body part. Patient nervousness can be contagious, but clinicians can relax patients by being comfortable themselves. A turning point involved a patient with an artificial bladder who kept ending up in the ICU because she did not understand she needed to catheterize regularly; she was doing it unpredictably, and the team initially missed the problem. The conclusion was clear: technical surgical success is meaningless if the patient does not understand how their life will change or what complications and side effects may occur.

That insight motivated her turn to YouTube. Academic research and dissemination can take five to ten years, while she wanted to improve health literacy faster. She committed to one video a week for six months and reached 1,000 subscribers, which she saw as powerful compared with the number of patients she could see in a clinic. A video about how to lengthen a penis received 30 million views. It was inspired by a systematic review on penile lengthening and discussed safer methods alongside methods that do not work. She notes that many men try to fix sexual problems themselves for a long time before seeking help, and that men may be dismissed by doctors when raising penis-size concerns. She states that 45% of men want to be taller, but even more want a larger penis. Her approach is harm reduction and informed choice, because dismissal pushes people toward snake oil or dangerous solutions.

Sexual health is framed as part of overall health. Sexual function reflects vascular, neurological, hormonal, and psychological systems, and untreated problems can cause depression, anxiety, and reduced productivity. Erectile dysfunction and related issues can signal broader health risks, including heart attacks, strokes, and dementia. A patient example involves a gym owner and entrepreneur who was doing many health-related things right but was stressed all the time, illustrating that people can overlook a major factor like stress while believing they are doing everything correctly.

Stress activates the sympathetic nervous system, but arousal requires the parasympathetic system, so constant stress makes it hard to be present for sex. A large study found people having sex about once a week had a 49% lower risk of death compared with those having sex about once a year. The speaker frames this as an association and a marker of overall health, not proof of longer lifespan, and clarifies the 49% figure as a difference in risk of death in a given year, not living 49% longer; an intermediate group had roughly 36% higher risk than the highest-frequency group. The study looked at people having sex generally, not specifically within relationships.

Standard medical-school questions about sexual activity are insufficient. Asking why someone is or is not having sex reveals treatable issues like pain, partner unwillingness, erectile difficulties, or loss of desire for something they used to enjoy. People often default to insecurity-based explanations rather than curiosity: men may assume their partner is unhappy without asking, and women may assume their partner no longer finds them attractive. Patients rarely volunteer sexual problems, so clinicians must ask or the issue goes unnoticed.

Vascular health is central to sexual health. Preventing high blood pressure, high cholesterol, and diabetes requires good fuel and healthy body weight. Diet rules emphasized include enough protein, enough fiber, at least 20% fat to make cholesterol and testosterone, and keeping calories in check. Certain foods are linked to reduced erectile dysfunction risk: flavonoids in fruits and vegetables, with blueberries cited as reducing risk by about 22%, and the Mediterranean diet showing about a 20% reduction. Nitrates from beets, arugula, and whole foods may help via nitric oxide, though the data is described as limited. Sleep apnea is strongly linked to poor erections and testosterone, partly because nighttime is when the body replenishes testosterone, and snoring is described as a strong sign of possible sleep apnea.

Erection mechanics are explained through nitric oxide release from healthy blood vessels and nerves. Blood vessels relax, blood flows into the penis, and spongy tissue expands in length and girth. The outer tunica expands and compresses veins so blood stays in; when the stimulus fades, blood flows out and detumescence occurs. Cardiovascular exercise is claimed to improve erectile function scores by a magnitude comparable to Viagra, about 150 to 160 minutes per week, with moderate intensity as the ideal target and walking acceptable for beginners. Strength training supports hormonal health, and training large muscle groups is linked to testosterone improvements; maintaining muscle mass is associated with better libido, erection quality, and satisfaction.

The pelvic floor is described as a muscular bowl supporting organs and playing a major role in sex, with rhythmic contractions during climax and, in men, pushing out ejaculate. Strong pelvic floor muscles are linked to stronger orgasms and more forceful ejaculation. Pelvic floor dysfunction can be hypertonic, stuck tight or shortened, causing urinary urgency, frequent urination, constipation, difficulty emptying the bladder, back and hip pain, pain with erections or ejaculation, scrotal pain, erection difficulty from reduced blood flow, and premature ejaculation. Relaxing a hypertonic pelvic floor is difficult because it is often unconscious and typically requires a pelvic floor physical therapist plus at-home stretches, yoga-type poses, and diaphragmatic breathing. Diaphragmatic breathing helps relax the pelvic floor and helps men last longer by keeping them in a calmer parasympathetic state.

High-intensity interval training may help with premature ejaculation by teaching awareness of triggers, heart-rate control, and recovery. A small Chinese study had men do seven minutes of high-intensity interval training daily for two weeks and measured intra-ejaculatory latency time; participants increased it by about 900%. Proposed mechanisms include balancing the nervous system and learning body cues by pushing hard then relaxing. Yoga and running also helped but took longer than two weeks. Erectile dysfunction is far more common in the patient population than premature ejaculation, with roughly 52% of men over 50 having erectile problems versus about 20% for premature ejaculation. Premature ejaculation carries more shame and less formal recognition, with no on-label medications and only off-label options such as SSRIs and Tramadol. Behavioral techniques include stop-start edging: reach near ejaculation, stop or squeeze the head of the penis, repeat three times, and allow ejaculation on the fourth.

Clinical premature ejaculation definition matters less than whether duration bothers the person or partner. Worldwide data measured by stopwatch during penetration only found average duration of about five to five and a half minutes. The goal of sex is pleasure; penetration does not always equal pleasure, and many people experience pleasure without penetration. Anxiety pushes people toward the sympathetic nervous system and accelerates arousal, which is offered as an explanation for why first-time sex can manifest differently for men and women. For women, anxiety can tense the pelvic floor and impede arousal; full arousal and lubrication takes about 25 minutes, during which the vagina widens and lengthens and the cervix moves up and out of the way, implying foreplay matters.

The body has three to five nighttime erections and three to five clitoral tumescences nightly, protecting itself even without sex or masturbation. A well-controlled study found men who ejaculated 21 or more times per month had lower prostate cancer rates than those who ejaculated four to seven times per month; the study did not distinguish masturbation from sex. One theory is that ejaculation clears the pipes and avoids stagnant ejaculatory fluid, but the speaker cautions against treating 21 times a month as a target. There is no correct amount of masturbation; the benchmark is that it is for pleasure and does not interfere with life or become obsessive. Masturbation begins variably; babies do it as self-soothing, and many people start around puberty.

Pornography is best framed like alcohol or drugs: the issue is frequency, context, and whether it becomes a coping mechanism rather than a source of pleasure. Moral incongruence, feeling that porn is bad, is cited as a factor that often makes use become a problem, and abstinence-only approaches have a higher failure rate than moderation-focused work. Problematic use is indicated by shame, avoiding responsibilities, preferring porn over a partner, or habituation that creates porn-related erectile dysfunction via neural pathways to specific arousal patterns. Porn is a major unintended sex educator for young people, with average access age cited as around 10, and many young men develop insecurity and distorted expectations because no one else is talking to them about sex. Porn producers use tricks and special effects to make scenes look different from reality.

Sexual confidence is defined as understanding a partner's anatomy, techniques, and erogenous zones, not just feeling like a good lover, and it requires ongoing effort to keep sex from becoming stale. Suggested novelty is small, about 4% harder, such as a different location, one arm on the bed, or a cushion; drastic purchases like swings are often bought but rarely used. Couples can fall apart while both suffer in silence. For many men, sex is the primary way they experience and display intimacy, so when it disappears much of the relationship feels lost to them. Men's not lasting long enough can stem from erectile dysfunction, with men rushing to climax before losing their erection, reinforcing fast muscle memory often learned through quick masturbation.

Women's low desire is complex and shaped by pain, hormonal changes, stress, and disproportionate household burdens. Scheduled sex creates performance pressure for men and consent pressure for women; scheduled intimacy, focused closeness without the expectation of sex, is offered as the better alternative. A recurring tension is that men tend to experience sex as stress relief while women often experience it as another task, even when they enjoy it. A sex shop owner reported that swings are frequently purchased but rarely used. A couple discussed, Kevin and Sandra, had not had sex for four years; Kevin was sad about lost intimacy, and his partner had untreated menopausal or perimenopausal changes causing pain or recurrent infections. Treating Kevin's erectile problems helped him last longer, and his partner's pain and desire issues were also addressed.

Two on-label desire medications are mentioned: Addyi, the little pink pill, taken nightly with effects after about three months, and Vyleesi, an injection taken 45 minutes before that works on melatonin receptors to increase dopamine. Addyi has been approved for postmenopausal women, and insurance coverage is described as challenging. Vyleesi can cause nausea, and the doctor advises taking an anti-nausea medication with it. Testosterone is used off-label for low desire, mostly studied in postmenopausal women, and declines slowly over time rather than dropping sharply. Viagra is framed as a bottom-up treatment acting on blood vessels, while desire medications work top-down on the brain. Responsive desire means that in long-term relationships desire often follows closeness and touch rather than preceding it, which differs from spontaneous desire. Suggested opening lines for a long-avoided conversation include telling a partner you love them, miss being close, and would like to talk when they feel ready. Advice includes having difficult conversations on a walk or in a car rather than face to face.

Penis size functions as an early, innate male status signal learned among boys. It is not correlated with skill as a lover or partner pleasure, and the fear around it is largely generated within the male gender rather than by women. Men can become excellent lovers through learned skill regardless of size. Botox injected into the penis is an off-label, emerging treatment for erectile dysfunction: it relaxes penile muscles so blood flows in more easily, and in small randomized studies helped some men with severe ED avoid implants or return to medication. Roughly 30% of men with severe ED saw improvement, some avoiding surgery, and Botox may increase flaccid penis length by about half a centimeter, though studies are very small. The theoretical risk is priapism, an erection lasting more than four hours, which is dangerous due to lack of blood flow; no cases have been reported. Botox is also used off-label for high-tone pelvic floor after physical therapy to relax muscles enough to benefit from therapy.

Psychological factors are present in virtually every erection problem, and placebo response is powerful, about 40% improvement on sugar pills in Viagra trials, which also explains perceived benefits from non-science-based supplements. Testosterone matters for symptoms like brain fog, depression, muscle and fat changes, ED, and low desire, but fixation on a single total number is misguided because individual androgen receptor sensitivity varies and some men feel fine at 300 to 320. Total testosterone can mislead because sex hormone binding globulin can capture it, leaving little free testosterone available to tissues. The speaker reports being on testosterone for about eight to nine years and having had high sex hormone binding globulin, leaving no free testosterone. Diminishing returns appear after optimal testosterone: muscle benefits may continue but stronger erections do not, and higher doses can cause erectile dysfunction via elevated estrogen. Testosterone use carries serious risks for young men, including infertility, testicular shrinkage, and difficulty recovering erections after stopping, and it is not reliable birth control. Sleep strongly affects testosterone: sleeping five hours versus eight hours dropped testosterone by about 15% in the same men, equivalent to roughly 15 years of age-related decline.

Male infertility is involved in about 50% of infertility cases and is easy to test for, including at-home kits; fever within the last three months can skew results, so two tests are recommended. Semen volume factors include hydration, longer abstinence between ejaculation, and Kegel exercises, which can make ejaculation more forceful and appear more voluminous. Squirting fluid includes dilute urine plus likely fluid from the Skene's glands, based on dye-in-bladder studies and chemical analysis showing dilute urine plus PSA. PSA in squirting fluid is linked to the Skene's glands, located under the urethra near the G-spot area. An estimate states that about 40% of females cannot squirt, based on limited research. Clitoris anatomy is described as the homologue of the penis, with internal corpora and shaft spreading out and only the glans externally visible; the shaft lies on the anterior side of the vagina. The clitoral hood is compared to the foreskin, can be pulled back and cleaned, and adhesions between hood and glans can cause discomfort or muted orgasms. Conventional in-and-out penetration is described as not optimal; angling and rocking techniques aimed at stimulating the clitoris are presented as better.

The book referenced uses a house metaphor with four pillars: fuel, strength, environment, and confidence. Fuel relates to you are what you eat, and the penis is described as a vascular organ. Environmental factors discussed include endocrine-disrupting chemicals, sleep, stress, masturbation, pornography, and social company. The company a person keeps shapes expectations about sex; being around people who have resigned themselves to sexless relationships can lead someone to accept the same rather than work at it. Pelvic floor issues are described as underdiagnosed, with many cases appearing during COVID due to prolonged sitting, reduced movement, and stress and anxiety, with patients referred to pelvic floor physical therapy. Kegels can increase pelvic floor strength and potentially produce more intense orgasms and more forceful ejaculate; warnings include stopping if pain or discomfort occurs and allowing rest days, since muscles can get stuck in a contracted state. The book includes a quick at-home exercise day and a relaxation day.

Study Notes - (Pulpit Version Explained) (PART A)
Psalms 141:1-10
EXPOSITION
ALMOST wholly a psalm of supplication. David is again in danger, and needs a prompt deliverance (Psa_141:1). This time the danger seems to be that he may fall away, and be absorbed into the company of the wicked. He therefore prays:
1. That prayer may be with him a settled institution (Psa_141:2).
2. That he may be saved from sins of the tongue (Psa_141:3).
3. That he may be saved from sins of thought or act (Psa_141:4).
4. That he may be given grace to welcome reproof (Psa_141:5).
The circumstances of the time are then shortly touched. There has been a severe judgment on the rulers of the people (Psa_141:6), and a great national calamity (Psa_141:7), with the result that the people are touched in their hearts, while David’s confidence in God is in no way diminished. This is followed by a renewal of prayer:
(1) for his own deliverance (Psa_141:9); and
(2) for a further punishment of the wicked (Psa_141:10).
Psa_141:1
Lord, I cry unto thee; make haste unto me. The need is pressing and urgent. God is therefore entreated to "hasten" (comp. Psa_22:19; Psa_31:2; Psa_38:22; Psa_40:17, etc.). Give ear unto my voice, when I cry unto thee (comp. Psa_102:2).
Psa_141:2
Let my prayer be set forth (or, "established") before thee as incense; i.e. with the regularity of the incense, and with its acceptableness. And the lifting up of my hands as the evening sacrifice. The hands were "lifted up" in prayer, which was reckoned a serf of sacrifice (Hos_14:2).
Psa_141:3
Set a watch, O Lord, before my mouth; keep the door of my lips (comp. Psa_39:1). David’s was a hasty, impetuous temper, which required sharp control. He strove to "keep his own mouth with a bridle"—to " be dumb with silence, and hold his peace"—but this was not always possible for him of his own unassisted strength. He therefore makes his prayer to God for the Divine help.
Psa_141:4
Incline not my heart to any evil thing; i.e. let not my heart be inclined to any form of evil. To practice wicked works (rather, wicked practices) with men that work iniquity; and let me not eat of their dainties. Let me not be drawn in to their life of sinful luxury.
Psa_141:5
Let the righteous smite me; it shall be a kindness; rather, let the righteous smite me kindly, as in the margin. And let him reprove me; it shall be an excellent oil, which shall not break my head; rather, which my head shall not refuse. The psalmist will prefer the reproof of the righteous to the dainty allurements of the wicked. He will regard their words as an oil of welcome, such as was poured upon the head of favored guests (Luk_7:36), and his head will not refuse it. For yet my prayer also shall be in their calamities; rather, their wickednesses. This healing oil will strengthen him to continue to pray for his enemies, even though they still continue in their "wickednesses."
Psa_141:6
When their judges are overthrown in stony places, they shall hear my words. Calamity opens the heart to receive instruction. The "judges"—i.e. the leaders—among David’s enemies are visited with a grievous calamity, expressed metaphorically by their being dashed upon rocks. This disposes them to listen to David’s words, which are well worth listening to, since they are sweet.
Psa_141:7
Our bones are scattered at the grave’s mouth. The calamity is not confined to the "judges." The bones of the people generally lie scattered at hews mouth—unburied, i.e; but ready to go down to Hades. As when one cutteth and cleaveth wood upon the earth; rather, as when one cleaves and breaks up the earth. "The bones of God’s servants were strewn as thickly ever the ground as stones over a newly ploughed piece of soil, so that the Holy Land looked as if it had become an antechamber of Hades" (Kay).
Psa_141:8
But mine eyes are unto thee, O God the Lord. I, however, the psalmist says, do not despair—I look to thee, O Jehovah the Lord (comp. Psa_40:7)—in thee is my trust; leave not my soul destitute. The last clause is, literally, pour not out my soul; i.e. destroy me not—do not spill my life on the ground (comp. Isa_53:12).
Psa_141:9
Keep me from the snares which they have laid for me, and the gins of the workers of iniquity (comp. Psa_40:4, Psa_40:5).
Psa_141:10
Let the wicked fall into their own nets (comp. Psa_7:15; Psa_35:8; Psa_57:6; Pro_5:22). The moral sense is always satisfied when the wicked man falls into his own trap, or is "hoist with his own petard." Even a heathen poet could say—
"Nec lex justior ulla est,
Quam necis artifices arte perire sun."
Whilst that I withal escape; literally, until that I pass over; i.e. whilst I pass over the nets, or traps, in safety.
HOMILETICS
Psa_141:1-10
Acceptable sacrifices.
The more distinctive teaching of this psalm respects—
I. THE SACRIFICE OF PRAYER. (Psa_141:2, Psa_141:8, Psa_141:9.) When the sacrificial services of the tabernacle (or temple) could not be rendered, it was open to the devout Israelite to "lift up his hands" in reverent, believing prayer. And this, we are sure, was acceptable to "him that heareth prayer." The essence of all sacrifice was an appeal to God by the spirit of man, the going forth of the human spirit to the Divine Spirit; it was this that was symbolized by the incense or slain lamb. The presentation of the visible meant and expressed the offering of that which was invisible—the grateful, or the penitent or the dedicatory thought and feeling of the worshipper. Prayer, therefore, was of the essential nature of a true sacrifice. We cannot offer, at any altar, anything which is more well pleasing to God than the prayer which "goeth not forth from feigned lips," which rises from the heart—the morning sacrifice of supplication for guidance and protection throughout the duties and difficulties and temptations of the day; the evening sacrifice of thanksgiving for the blessings that have been bestowed, of prayer for the forgiveness of imperfect service, and of trustful surrender of body and spirit to the Divine keeping for the coming night.
II. THE SACRIFICE OF SPEECH AND SILENCE. (Psa_141:3.) The psalmist prays God to "keep the door of his lips" (see Psa_34:13; Psa_39:1; Jas_3:3-12). It is well to ask God to do this, but it is also well to recognize that he requires of us that we should do this also. The use we make of our tongue, that member which is "our glory" (Psa_30:12; Psa_57:8), and too often is our shame, is a very serious and important feature of our Christian life.
1. By a determined silence when we are tempted to speak and to strike, we may save ourselves and others from a "fire" (Jas_3:6) which might desolate and destroy. He that "ruleth his spirit" and holdeth his tongue is a true conqueror (Pro_16:32).
2. And when we use our tongue to utter words of conciliation, to express regret for inadvertent error or omission, to excuse unintentional or pardonable faultiness, to pardon wrong, to encourage weakness, to enlighten ignorance, to impel to duty or devotion, to lead men in prayer to God, we are offering a very acceptable sacrifice—"the calves of our lips" (Hos_14:2).
III. THE SACRIFICE OF SEPARATION AND ABSTINENCE. If we pray (see Psa_141:4) to be delivered from an inclination to join the wicked in their evil courses and in their ungodly revelries, we must exercise in ourselves a strong restraint; we must resolve to "enter not into the path of the wicked," to "turn from it and pass away" (Pro_4:14, Pro_4:15). The duty of declining invitations from the unholy, of keeping away from the hearth and the table where nothing virtuous or valuable is to be gained, and where much that is most precious may be lost or injured, is a duty, a sacrifice, very needful to the young. Regard or disregard of it may make all the difference between life and death. A wise separateness from sin (2Co_6:17) will be a very acceptable sacrifice to him who is our thrice-holy Lord, will save us from a peril which has meant ruin to many who imagined themselves strong and safe, and will place us by the side of him who himself was "undefiled, separate from sinners" (Heb_7:26).
IV. THE SACRIFICE OF DOCILITY. (Psa_141:5.) "It is allowable to learn from an enemy." It is much more obviously right to learn from "the righteous;" and, though they speak reprovingly and reflect on what we have said or done, their words should be well received.
1. The correction of man may be, in truth, the guidance of God. He may be speaking to us through his servants; it has often been the case with others, and it may well be so with us. It may be a Samuel, or an Elijah, or a Nathan, or a Paul that is speaking in God’s name.
2. We acknowledge ourselves to be in error, to be at fault, generally: why should we be unwilling to learn when we are so in particular instances!
3. The docile reception of rebuke may save us from much graver sorrow that we should otherwise suffer; it may result in an improvement of conduct and enlargement of usefulness for which we shall give God heartiest thanks.
HOMILIES BY S. CONWAY
Psa_141:1-10
Keep me from the snares.
This difficult psalm seems to be the cry of a greatly tempted soul. And the temptation now did not arise so much from the persecutions of the ungodly as from their seducing favors—what he calls "their dainties" (Psa_141:4). And he seems to have found this even harder to resist than their cruelty and harshness. Consider—
I. THE SPIRIT OF THIS PRAYER.
1. Note its impassioned earnestness. (Psa_141:1.) "Lord, I cry unto thee." No mere formal, ordinary prayer, but a pleading cry.
2. He pleads for haste on the part of the Lord. He can bear no delay.
3. That his cry may find much acceptance. (Psa_141:2.) The burning of incense was one chief part of the evening sacrifice, and the meaning of it was to set forth, by its fragrance and sweet odor, the acceptableness of sincere believing prayer. Hence the psalmist here seeks that his cry may be thus acceptable before God.
II. ITS SUBSTANCE. His enemies, by bribes, favors, and blandishments of one kind and another, are seeking to lead him astray from God. Hence he prays:
1. That he may not commit himself by rash and unguarded speech. (Psa_141:3.) What a peril and a snare this is to many! How often have they found themselves entrapped and entangled by some hasty utterance, which should never have passed their lips! These doors open too quickly and too easily, and let out what should be kept in; they need a watchman to guard them and to determine when they shall or shall not be opened, and only the Lord can set that watch. Happy the man for whom he does this!
2. That his heart may be kept true. (Psa_141:4.) It is a blessed thing when our external conduct is kept right, when our hands are tied by God’s providence, and so held in from mischief; but it is better far when our hearts are made right, so that they will have no desire for evil things. And God will do this for us. "The blood of Jesus Christ … cleanseth from all sin."
3. That the dainties of the wicked may not seduce him. Thus do they persuade men of unstable mind to practice wicked works. The way is smoothed, made to seem so attractive and right, just as our first parents were tempted, for theirs was the pattern of all successful temptation. The devil has great store of these "dainties;" he knows how to suit all tastes and to please all palates.
4. That he may not lack a faithful reprover. (Psa_141:5.) There are plentiful prophets who will prophesy smooth things for the sin-loving soul; but faithful Micaiahs (1Ki_22:8) are few and far between. But the psalmist here prays that he may never want for such. Let us pray the little prayer. How many go wrong just for want of such faithful reproof! Those who should reprove often shrink from their duty, for it is the reverse of pleasant.
5. That his soul may not perish. (Psa_141:8.) That its life may not be poured out,—such is the meaning of the word; emptied as a vessel. He was in sore peril; his enemies by "their dainties" were devising all manner of stratagem against him—snares, gins, nets.
6. That in spite of all, he may escape.
III. HIS CONFIDENT HOPE. (Psa_141:6.) That when the leaders, the rulers and judges, who led the way in wickedness,—when they were hurled down the rock (cf. 2Ch_25:12; 2Ki_9:33), then their followers would hear his words and welcome them. Let the ringleaders be got out of the way; the rest would gladly listen to godly counsels. And these leaders in evil deserved such doom; for they had been cruel persecutors of the people of God (Psa_141:7), whose bones were scattered along the borders of the grave in vast numbers, like so many furrows made by the plough. And for such turning of the hearts of the people and for his own escape from his present trial he would continually wait on God, for God was his trust (Psa_141:8). Hence he confidently hoped to see the wicked leaders destroyed, their followers converted, and his own soul kept by the grace of God. Such prayers will ever inspire such hopes.—S.C.
Psa_141:3
Keep the door of my lips.
How needed is a sentinel and guard at the door! For lack of it, what mischief has been wrought! Who can recount all the ills of unguarded speech?
I. LIP-SINS: THEIR CAUSE.
1. Impulsive temperament. Like as a stroke from the whip, which would only make the common cart-horse slowly shake his head, but would send the thorough-bred flying over the hedge in a very tornado of rage, so there are men who are never roused to hasty speech, they never get into trouble that way; whilst others, quick-witted, agile-minded, swift to see what can be said on any given subject,—they are apt to think that all that can be said must be said, and with sad unwisdom they haste to say it. These are the "good talkers;" unhappy ones, they should rather be called.
2. Vanity. A liking to show off, coupled with the consciousness that they can do so if they choose.
3. Want of self-control. There are times when even cautious, well-balanced men are driven out of their wonted self-restraint, so great is the provocation they have received; but there are others who never seem to put any check upon themselves, but yield to every impulse and follow at once every prompting of their uncontrolled thoughts; they need no great provocation, but will pour out their multitude of words on any and every occasion, whether wise or otherwise.
4. Evil temper and mere thoughtlessness are other causes of much of the unguarded and hasty speech with which the world is afflicted; and so is:
5. The lack of real religion, of the fear of God, and of the sense of the seriousness of life and conduct.
II. THEIR CONSEQUENCES.
1. To the speaker himself.
(1) "In the multitude of words there wanteth not sin." The man who lets his tongue run on unrestrained is sure to say something that will bring guilt on his soul and burden on his conscience.
(2) Weakening of the character and will. The invaluable blessing of strength of will is only won by diligent self-restraint and watchful self-recollection; but it is sapped and wasted by unguarded and multitudinous speech.
(3) Loss of reputation. Men reckon one another up, and a man of many words never wins their confidence; they almost instinctively distrust him. Thus the man may do himself real harm, and lessen his influence, and misrepresent his own character.
(4) Such loose unrestrained talk rarely bears reflection; it is generally followed by much regret and sadness and repentance.
2. To the hearer of such unguarded speech. Great harm may be done. "You drop, in the thoughtlessness of conversation, or for the sake of argument or wit, some irreligious, skeptical expression; it lodges in the memory of a child or a servant; it takes root in a soil favorable to such seed; it gradually springs up and brings forth fruit in disregard of religious duty, neglect of the means of grace, and the various steps of a downward course, the end of which no one can tell. This is all too common a case. But there is a Being who knows where it began." We little know what great things from little ones may rise. And how often, in loose unrestrained speech, we inflict cruel and needless pain I We did not think to do harm, but it is done all the same. And what an ill example we set to those who hear us; and one so apt to be followed!
3. And to those spoken of. They are likely to be misrepresented. From careless good nature we may commend some who, if we do not censure and warn against them, we, at least, should be silent concerning them. Or, on the other hand, and a more likely case, those of whom we speak so carelessly are likely to be injured, and perhaps seriously, and a false impression given of them, which they by no means deserve. How repeatedly the Scriptures give warning on this subject (see Pro_18:21; Pro_15:2, Pro_15:7; Mat_13:36, Mat_13:37; Jas_1:26, etc.)!
III. ITS CURE.
1. Prayer. The text is a prayer. It will be God’s special grace that alone can conquer this too common sin.
2. Cultivate the habit of thoughtfulness and self-recollection. Lift up your heart to God for his aid in this matter, when you go into company where temptation to this sin is likely to beset you.
3. Vows of silence for given periods. These will tend to strengthen the habit of self-control.
4. Seek and cherish love to your fellow-men—to do to them as you would they should do to you.
5. And because as the tree is so will be its fruits, therefore seek the grace of God, that you yourself may be possessed and sanctified and kept of the Holy Spirit. Then shall ways and works and words be alike good.—S.C.
Psa_141:5
The excellent oil of reproof; or, kindness smiting.
Much may be learned from this verse concerning the very difficult and delicate task of reproving others. We learn—
I. THAT REPROOF MAY BE SO ADMINISTERED AS TO BE EVEN WELCOMED. "Let the righteous smite me," etc.; and further down in the verse, "Let not my head refuse it;" such is the truer rendering of the Revised Version in the clause which our Authorized Version reads, "which shall not break my head." It is evident, therefore, that the reproving told of here was not hated and resented, as reproof commonly is, but even gratefully accepted. Generally, as we know, reproof is amongst the most unpalatable of things (see an admirable sermon by C.H. Spurgeon on Job_6:6). And we know this, and therefore needed rebuke and admonition are not given as they should be. We too often see our brother go wrong, and out of craven fear we hold back the warning and the reproof.
II. AND THIS, NOTWITHSTANDING IT MAY BE SEVERE. The psalmist calls it a smiting: "Let the righteous smite me." And on the head also; for he says (Revised Version), "Let not my head refuse it." A blow on the body would be far less injurious, painful, and ignominious than one on the head, such as is contemplated here. But still it is welcomed. This is difficult when "the righteous one" is God, who, as some expositors affirm, is here meant (see 2Sa_7:14, 2Sa_7:15). To humble ourselves under even his mighty hand (Heb_12:5-11), to whom we should "much rather be in subjection," is often found far from easy by our rebellions hearts; but if "the righteous" spoken of be our fellow-men, then it is more difficult still. But here such smiting is not only submitted to, but welcomed. This is a very unusual thing indeed.
III. FURTHERMORE, IT SHALL BE DEEMED "KINDNESS," AND GRATEFUL AS "THE OIL OF JOY." For this is what is here referred to (cf. Psa_23:5; Psa_45:7; Mat_6:17). His soul is glad because of it; he counts himself happy and fortunate to have received it. How is all this to be understood? Therefore note—
IV. THE EXPLANATION OF SUCH RARE RECEPTION OF REPROOF.
1. Certainly it is not because the man is mean-spirited and lies down like a slave or a stricken dog to be beaten. It is no "Uriah Heep" kind of humility. If we thought that such language as we have here would be nauseating, we should, as we ought, despise it.
2. But the evident explanation of it is that the man’s whole soul longed after holiness and purity, and loathed sin with a great loathing. He so dreaded being betrayed into sin, that he welcomed with joy any rebuke, no matter how severe and shameful, that restrained him from it. Thus is this strong, strange speech explained.
3. And what a revelation of the grace of God in a man’s soul it is! Oh to so hate sin that we shall be glad of any suffering, yea, death itself, rather than come under its power! Happy the heart that can say "Amen" to the psalmist’s prayer!
V. THE REPROVER AND THE REPROOF.
1. The reprover. He must be righteous and felt to be so by him whom he reproves. It is not, "Let anybody reprove me," but "the righteous." Reproof from others would be of no avail. But the righteous reprover is one who knows that what he says is true, that reproof ought to be given, because a brother’s soul is in peril. Also he is one who feels deeply the dread evil of sin; it is no trifle to him, whether in himself or others; the honor of God is dear to him, and so is his brother’s soul. For he not only feels, but loves. That is the motive which urges him, apart from which he would have said nothing. Such are the characteristics of the righteous reprover.
2. And then, the reproof. The similitude here employed—the fragrant, refreshing, healthful anointing oil—suggests much. As to the gentleness of the reproof. Though the psalmist says he would welcome it though it were as a smiting on the head, it need not, should not, will not, be like that (see our Savior’s reproofs of his disciples, Mat_26:41). And as to its insinuating, penetrating power, not by its harshness, but the very reverse. And as to its being much mingled with love and evident kindness of heart. Reprove so; for such reproof will not repel, but rather bind yet more closely to you the heart of him whom you reprove. See what he says, "For yet my prayer also shall be in their calamities." We prefer this rendering; it tells how the psalmist loved the righteous ones who had reproved him, and would still pray for them amid their sorrow: they might say anything to him, it would not sever his soul from theirs.—S.C.
Psa_141:5
Praying for others.
The psalmist here says he will do this. We need not trouble about the right rendering of this difficult verse, but may take it as it stands. It says that the calamities of the righteous shall stir the psalmist’s soul to pray for them. He loved them much, even though they severely rebuked him, indeed, because they did so.
I. IT IS A BEAUTIFUL EXAMPLE. We pray for ourselves, and it is right we should, for unless we ourselves are right with God we shall care but little for the highest good of others, and we shall be disqualified for interceding for them. How ungodly parents who, nevertheless, love their children very dearly, should remember this! They cannot render their children the highest service of all until they themselves are reconciled to God. But we ought not to pray only for ourselves. We can be selfish even in prayer; it is to be feared we very often are. But selfishness is as wrong there as elsewhere.
II. IT HAS THE HIGHEST SANCTION. Our Lord Jesus Christ now at the right hand of God "ever liveth to make intercession for us." Moreover, he has taught us to pray, "Our Father, which art," etc. It is not "my:" our Lord would have us be intercessors for others when we pray for ourselves.
III. THERE ARE INNUMERABLE REASONS FOR IT.
1. It is part of our obedience to Christ. We are to love our neighbor as ourselves. Surely this includes prayer for him.
2. It unites us with Christ. We cannot "redeem our brother or give to God a ransom for him;" but we can pray for him.
3. It does such good.
(1) To those we pray for. We may be sure that God never draws forth our hearts in fervent prayer for others, and then disappoints that prayer. See Abraham’s intercession for Sodom. How much do not we ourselves owe to those that have prayed for us! Saintly fathers and mothers, holy men and ministers of God, asked for our salvation, and it has been given. What a motive this for like prayer on our own part! What faithful preacher does not know that his congregation’s preparedness to receive the Word is largely in proportion to the fervency of his prayers!
(2) And to ourselves who pray, such prayer is blessed. It clears our minds of ill will; it prompts us to kindly, helpful thought, word, and deed; it wins the smile of God on our own souls.
4. It is a work we can all engage in, though we may not be able to do much else. What do not the ministers of God owe to poor bed-ridden people who pray for them as they minister!—S.C.
Psa_141:7, Psa_141:8
The victory of faith.
In these verses two contrasted scenes are set before us. We are shown—

#SME #TechEra #TechEraEngineering #TechEraEngineeringIndia

TechEra Engineering (India) H1 FY27 Concall Highlights:

👉H1 FY27 & Future Outlook :
▫️FY27 outlook: growth on the positive side, but slightly conservative
💠Revenue growth could be ~15%, ~20% or potentially reach 30%
💠Earlier 30% growth is a steep task now, though not ruled out
💠Profitability to stay positive on a full-year basis; no PAT or PBT number given
💠H2 expected to be better than H1

▫️Inventory build-up to convert into revenue within ~6 months, and before March 2027
💠Project-based business with long proving cycles; projects planned for 6–7 months can stretch by a couple of months until proving is done

▫️H1 FY27 financials: revenue of ~₹22 Cr, lower than H1 FY26
💠Employee cost rose sharply as people were hired and trained ahead of new capability and opportunities
💠Two or three new initiatives for the private sector (flying parts and insourcing) held H1 back slightly
💠No deliberate delay in execution and no order shortfall; delays were routine data exchanges, customer inspections and part trials
💠Management said it understands the reasons for the H1 numbers and how they will be rectified

▫️FY28 and FY29 projections unchanged
💠Growth is still expected but has been pushed out by a couple of years, as the Indian Air Force took 1.5–2 years just to evaluate a new supplier
💠Initiatives taken now are meant to carry the experience needed for FY28 and FY29 opportunities
💠Employee cost increase to be far smaller than the rise in revenue after 6–12 months; headcount to stabilise

▫️Long-term EBITDA margin: 17–20% on average, reviewed every 6 months based on the work mix

▫️Capacity: current set-up can support ₹100–120 Cr of revenue without fresh capex
💠Capex only if new capabilities are needed (aircraft engine plates, blades, titanium machining); one machine costs ₹5–6 Cr
💠Machinery upgrades every ~6 months to attract bigger clients

▫️Debt: plan to address the balance sheet through profitability over the next 2–3 years; no commitment on a quick reduction

👉Order book / projects and pipeline:
▫️Order book: ~₹55–57 Cr, nearly ₹60 Cr
💠Spread across tooling and fixtures, flying parts and insourcing
💠~60% to be executed within the year and ~40% in the next financial year
💠Order book has grown 20–30% each time it has been updated (every 4–6 months); same pace expected

▫️Bid pipeline:
💠Proposals submitted run in three figures at all times; conversion timing cannot be predicted
💠Majority of bids are under customer technical review
💠Competing with tier 1s and OEMs that are building similar capability

▫️Indian Air Force (direct orders):
💠Two orders won, including a development-cum-production order for an electrical coolanol unit; the first was very small and took 1.5 years, the second took 4–5 months and is substantial
💠Winning gives a 5-year arrangement under which IAF units across India can order directly
💠Third and fourth orders being pursued; several quotations submitted; process is by invitation after technical vetting, unlike open GeM tenders
💠Many such development and design projects would create revenue every six months, alongside project-based work

▫️HAL aircraft programmes (LCA Tejas Mk1, HTT-40 and others):
💠HAL has an LCA Tejas Mk1 order book of ~200 aircraft; TechEra makes more than 250 components and tooling for it
💠Parts ordered for 15 aircraft so far; TechEra gets first right of refusal for parts it has already made
💠Deliveries of the first 10–12 sets completed for one component; customer wants more, expected in Dec–Jan
💠Follow-on pricing is open to negotiation and expected to be higher than the first order
💠Supplying entire central fuselage and vertical stabiliser assemblies to HAL; capability building with HAL in progress

▫️Flying parts directory:
💠~275–300 varieties, 3,500–4,000 quantity; 25–30% of parts are made by no one else in the country, as single source
💠Directory to be shown to private commercial customers; entry into Airbus and Boeing supply within about a year
💠FY28 opportunities being bid for these single-source parts

▫️MRO and GSE:
💠MRO to be a large contributor, mainly from the Indian Air Force; two part numbers guaranteed, more being added
💠No H1/H2 split given; update expected in H2
💠Couple of new GSE customers added

▫️Export: one export order already declared; more export orders expected soon
💠Capability built is expected to draw buyers from abroad

▫️Aircraft-making vision: 8–10 years away

👉Q&A :
▫️Growth guidance and promoter stake sale:
💠No further stake will be sold by the promoter; any change would only come through a preferential issue, possibly to increase holding
💠Management recognised that investors are disheartened and said it is geared to turn things around

▫️Funding position:
💠Operations can meet financial obligations; any fundraising would be project-based, for capability or plant infrastructure

▫️Certifications:
💠Nadcap is not a priority; it can be obtained in 3–4 months if needed, and approved suppliers can do the special processes meanwhile

▫️Pricing:
💠Order for immediate delivery may be at the same price; later orders will be renegotiated

👉 Others :
▫️Management: Meet Desai (Whole-Time Director) took over as CFO; the earlier finance head continues
💠A new Independent Director has been appointed

▫️Customer and country: MD currently abroad for a customer meeting; country not disclosed

𝐃𝐄𝐌𝐎𝐂𝐑𝐀𝐓𝐒 𝐒𝐓𝐀𝐂𝐊𝐄𝐃 𝐀𝐋𝐀𝐒𝐊𝐀’𝐒 𝐁𝐀𝐋𝐋𝐎𝐓 𝐖𝐈𝐓𝐇 𝐀 𝐅𝐀𝐊𝐄 “𝐃𝐄𝐂𝐎𝐘 𝐃𝐀𝐍” — 𝐀𝐍𝐃 𝐒𝐓𝐈𝐋𝐋 𝐅𝐋𝐈𝐏𝐏𝐄𝐃 𝐓𝐇𝐄 𝐒𝐄𝐀𝐓

Democrat Mary Peltola has officially flipped a Republican-held Senate seat in Alaska, defeating incumbent Dan Sullivan 50.1% to 45.8% after a two-week count of nearly 288,000 ballots. President Trump called the scheme that helped get her there exactly what it was: “𝘴𝘰𝘭𝘦𝘭𝘺 𝘧𝘰𝘳 𝘵𝘩𝘦 𝘱𝘶𝘳𝘱𝘰𝘴𝘦 𝘰𝘧 𝘧𝘳𝘢𝘶𝘥 𝘢𝘯𝘥 𝘤𝘰𝘯𝘧𝘶𝘴𝘪𝘰𝘯.”

A retired Petersburg schoolteacher who shares the senator’s exact name, Dan J. Sullivan, ran as a self-described “𝘱𝘳𝘢𝘨𝘮𝘢𝘵𝘪𝘤 𝘙𝘦𝘱𝘶𝘣𝘭𝘪𝘤𝘢𝘯 𝘤𝘦𝘯𝘵𝘳𝘪𝘴𝘵” upset with the president. The New York Times later reported it had viewed texts and documents showing Peltola campaign staff, Democratic Senatorial Campaign Committee officials, and an operative who traveled Alaska under a false name worked to recruit him — specifically to confuse Republican voters staring at two Dan Sullivans on their ballot.

The decoy pulled 𝟒,𝟕𝟔𝟎 𝐯𝐨𝐭𝐞𝐬, and a second recruited spoiler named Gerald Heikes siphoned off another 6,105 — votes that never had a chance to reach the real Sullivan. Peltola’s campaign denied any role in the plot even as the Justice Department asked a federal court to be ready to delay certification if the confusion swung the outcome.

Peltola spent the campaign branding herself a moderate, claiming she opposed boys competing in girls’ sports and backed border security and Alaska’s oil industry. Her actual voting record tells a different story: she voted against the Protection of Women and Girls in Sports Act, the bill that would have banned exactly what she claimed to oppose. Sullivan’s campaign didn’t mince words: “𝘵𝘩𝘦 𝘴𝘢𝘮𝘦 𝘋.𝘊. 𝘭𝘢𝘸𝘺𝘦𝘳𝘴 𝘸𝘩𝘰 𝘴𝘱𝘦𝘯𝘵 𝘮𝘰𝘳𝘦 𝘵𝘩𝘢𝘯 𝘢 𝘺𝘦𝘢𝘳 𝘤𝘰𝘯𝘴𝘱𝘪𝘳𝘪𝘯𝘨 𝘸𝘪𝘵𝘩 𝘔𝘢𝘳𝘺 𝘗𝘦𝘭𝘵𝘰𝘭𝘢’𝘴 𝘤𝘢𝘮𝘱𝘢𝘪𝘨𝘯 𝘵𝘰 𝘥𝘦𝘤𝘦𝘪𝘷𝘦 𝘈𝘭𝘢𝘴𝘬𝘢𝘯 𝘷𝘰𝘵𝘦𝘳𝘴 𝘢𝘳𝘦 𝘯𝘰𝘸 𝘢𝘴𝘬𝘪𝘯𝘨 𝘢 𝘤𝘰𝘶𝘳𝘵 𝘵𝘰 𝘭𝘦𝘵 𝘩𝘦𝘳 𝘤𝘢𝘮𝘱𝘢𝘪𝘨𝘯 𝘪𝘨𝘯𝘰𝘳𝘦 𝘈𝘭𝘢𝘴𝘬𝘢 𝘭𝘢𝘸 𝘢𝘯𝘥 𝘤𝘩𝘢𝘯𝘨𝘦 𝘵𝘩𝘦 𝘳𝘶𝘭𝘦𝘴 𝘸𝘩𝘪𝘭𝘦 𝘷𝘰𝘵𝘦𝘴 𝘢𝘳𝘦 𝘴𝘵𝘪𝘭𝘭 𝘣𝘦𝘪𝘯𝘨 𝘤𝘰𝘶𝘯𝘵𝘦𝘥.”

This was already 𝐭𝐡𝐞 𝐦𝐨𝐬𝐭 𝐞𝐱𝐩𝐞𝐧𝐬𝐢𝐯𝐞 𝐒𝐞𝐧𝐚𝐭𝐞 𝐫𝐚𝐜𝐞 𝐢𝐧 𝐀𝐥𝐚𝐬𝐤𝐚’𝐬 𝐡𝐢𝐬𝐭𝐨𝐫𝐲, and it handed Democrats the seat that gives them a 𝟓𝟔-𝟒𝟒 𝐒𝐞𝐧𝐚𝐭𝐞 𝐦𝐚𝐣𝐨𝐫𝐢𝐭𝐲 in January — the first Alaska Senate win for their party since 2014. Trump and JD Vance both flew to Alaska to campaign for Sullivan in a state Trump carried by 13 points, and it still wasn’t enough to stop a ballot built, by the Times’ own reporting, to trick Republican voters. Your Senate majority was decided by a decoy.

𝐃𝐞𝐦𝐨𝐜𝐫𝐚𝐭𝐬 𝐝𝐢𝐝𝐧’𝐭 𝐰𝐢𝐧 𝐀𝐥𝐚𝐬𝐤𝐚 — 𝐭𝐡𝐞𝐲 𝐦𝐚𝐧𝐮𝐟𝐚𝐜𝐭𝐮𝐫𝐞𝐝 𝐜𝐨𝐧𝐟𝐮𝐬𝐢𝐨𝐧 𝐚𝐧𝐝 𝐜𝐚𝐥𝐥𝐞𝐝 𝐢𝐭 𝐚𝐧 𝐞𝐥𝐞𝐜𝐭𝐢𝐨𝐧.

text:
Garten sworn in as Senate President Pro Tempore

STATEHOUSE (Nov. 17, 2026) — State Sen. Chris Garten (R-Charlestown) was sworn in as the Indiana Senate President Pro Tempore today at the Statehouse during Organization Day – the ceremonial start of the 125th Indiana General Assembly. He was sworn into this leadership role by Indiana Supreme Court Chief Justice Loretta Rush.

Garten's swearing-in comes on the heels of unfounded legal challenges to his election as a state senator, as ruled by the Indiana Supreme Court unanimously. Garten decried the attempt to throw the Senate District 45 election results into chaos, citing the danger to every other elected official if judges were to become the arbiters of election results without first allowing election processes established in law to play out. Garten added that, had the unfounded legal challenge succeeded, the constituents of Senate District 45 would have been left without representation in the Indiana Senate.

"An order preventing a senator-elect from taking office raises fundamental questions about the separation of powers, the authority of our courts, and the constitutional responsibility of the Indiana Senate to judge the elections and qualifications of its members," Garten said. "In my view, these actions created unnecessary election chaos and brought Indiana to the brink of a constitutional confrontation over a disputed election."

Garten was seated and elected unanimously as Senate President Pro Tempore by the Indiana Senate in accordance with the Indiana Constitution and state law, and in full compliance with Senate Rules.

During the first session of each General Assembly, lawmakers craft a comprehensive budget to fund government services for the next two fiscal years. Garten pledged to scrutinize every taxpayer dollar and ensure government programs are run effectively and efficiently.

"It's time to get to work for Hoosiers tackling important issues like affordability, public safety, lower health care costs, improving education and ensuring every Hoosier has the chance to succeed," Garten said. "Senate Republicans bring a wealth of life of life experience and education to the Senate, and I've directed our members to focus on results over rhetoric in order to make material improvements in the lives of Hoosiers."

Organization Day includes the swearing in of new and re-elected members of the General Assembly. This day also marks the annual first roll call of all state lawmakers and gives each Senate and House of Representatives caucus the opportunity to organize in preparation for the 2027 legislative session. By state law, the 2027 session will conclude on or before April 29.

As the 2027 session gets underway, Garten encourages residents of Senate District 45 to contact him with any questions or comments they may have. Garten can be reached by filling out a "Contact Me" form at https://t.co/nTW6cmS10z or by phone at 800-382-9467.

State lawmakers will reconvene in January for the first regular session of the 125th General Assembly.

Restored plants now give the state an installed capacity of 552.34 million litres a day, the test now is whether it reaches every tap.

By Mukhtar Indabawa

For years, a running tap in Kano was a matter of luck; Households across the old city and the newer layouts rationed water, paid vendors and waited for pumps that failed or were not certain, the system behind those taps had been run down for a long time, Plants worked below their designed capacity, and pumping stations and mains sat idle or in disrepair. Pipes that went unused deteriorated further. When Governor Abba Kabir Yusuf took office in May 2023, much of that infrastructure needed rehabilitation or restoration before it could carry a drop of treated water.

The Ministry of Water Resources' own list of works shows how deep the neglect ran; The raw-water pump station at Tamburawa had to be restored, the main pipeline to Dambatta from the Thomas Water Treatment Plant needed rehabilitation, as did the Kusalla Regional Water Supply Scheme, the Wudil and Watari schemes. 

The Bagauda and Tudun Wada dams were in such a state that they had to be rehabilitated, Even the hydrology o at New Tamburawa. It supplied aluminium sulphate and Superflox polymer, along with other treatment chemicals, to the Challawa, Tamburawa, Watari and Kusalla plants. 

It provided fuel and AGO on monthly basis to the Kano State Water Board, as well as diesel for treatment plants and regional schemes. It also settled outstanding electricity bills at Challawa, Tamburawa, Watari, Kusalla and Wudil, and at the Board's headquarters.

On the network, the state laid a 1,000mm ductile-iron main from Tamburawa to Hadejia Road and extended Greater Kano supply to Goron Dutse and Mandawari, it also connected Sheka, Hotoro, Yan Shana, Unguwar Rimi, Naibawa and Unguwar Uku Yan Awaki.

Beyond the pipes, in its quest to provide and supply adequate water, the administration of Gov. Abba Kabir drilled 138 hand-pump boreholes under PEWASH and installed solar-powered boreholes in Kano Municipal, Gaya, Karaye, Kumbotso, Makoda and Minjibir, Ungogo also received a solar borehole with a 2,000-litre overhead tank. 

The Bagauda and Tudun Wada dams were rehabilitated, and design work and a topographic survey were completed for the proposed Kantama Earth Dam. The Reach-Out Water Supply Project now covers 20 communities.

The result is an installed capacity of 552.34 MLD, or 552,340,000 litres a day, across 22 treatment plants, regional schemes and booster stations. Three plants carry most of it; Challawa produces 220 MLD, Tamburawa 150 MLD and Watari 75 MLD, which together account for about 81 percent of the total - Wudil and Kafinchiri add 20 MLD each, and Kusalla adds 15 MLD, Joda, Guzuguzu, Tiga-Rano and Pada range from 6.4 to 9.6 MLD. Smaller schemes and boosters, from Ghari and Magaga to Bunkure and Falgore, supply the remaining 35.54 MLD.

Capacity, though, is not delivery, the government has acknowledged that test runs at Challawa and Tamburawa exposed weaknesses in the distribution network - reticulation, partly because the pipes had gone unused for so long. Those gaps are now being repaired, finding them was necessary, but fixing them is what residents will judge.

Sustaining the system matters as much as building it - Accordingly, the administration has pledged to establish a durable maintenance framework, ensure predictable operational funding and strengthen technical capacity, so that future governments inherit functional water facilities rather than another cycle of rehabilitation costs. 

Crucially, these commitments must be institutionalised to endure beyond 2031, Citizens, on their part, also have a responsibility to protect pipelines and boreholes against vandalism and other forms of damages.

Across benefiting communities, dry taps are gradually giving way to running water. The task ahead is to close the remaining distribution gaps, strengthen the reliability of the supply network and make access to safe, dependable water a lasting reality for every Kano resident. Ultimately, this is the promise of a Kano that puts its people first in all its dealings.

On Thursday, the leaders of the world's three largest nuclear arsenals meet at one table for the first time ever, with no US-Russia arms treaty in force. Here's what the numbers show. 🇺🇸🇨🇳🇷🇺

📊 The numbers
• Military stockpiles, January 2026: Russia about 4,400, the US about 3,700, China about 620. China is up from about 600 a year earlier, and it's the fastest-growing arsenal (SIPRI Yearbook 2026)
• Total inventories, including retired warheads: Russia 5,420, US 5,042, China 620. The US and Russia hold almost 86% of all the world's warheads (SIPRI)
• New START, the last US-Russia arms treaty, expired Feb 5, 2026. No extension or replacement is in force, so there are no binding caps, inspections or data exchanges. Russia says it will keep observing the old limits of 1,550 deployed warheads as long as the US does; IISS says neither side has moved to exceed those limits, but the restraint is informal and unverified
• APEC's 21 economies: about 62% of world GDP and 48% of world trade (APEC, 2021 data)
• The US-China trade truce that cut tariffs after last year's APEC was extended to January 2027 (CNBC)

• White House: Trump will raise the "reduction of nuclear weapons" at the trilateral, "among other topics" (assistant press secretary Olivia Wales, via SCMP)

✅ The facts
• China's Foreign Ministry confirmed the "China-Russia-U.S. Summit" for Nov 19 in Shenzhen. The White House and the Kremlin confirmed it too. The White House schedule lists it at 3:30 p.m. JST Thursday (2:30 p.m. in Shenzhen) at Kylin Villa (TASS)

• Trump and Xi are expected to hold their third summit this year. US officials say the talks will focus on putting the trade deal into practice, not on Nvidia (CNBC)
• Japan's PM Takaichi is expected at the leaders' meeting on her first China trip as PM. Elon Musk is set to travel with Trump (CNBC)

text:
A Jewish Holocaust Scholar Called Gaza a Genocide. He Lost His University Job Offer. Now the University Has Paid Him $250,000.

Raz Segal is an Israeli-American Jewish historian.

He is also the grandson of four Holocaust survivors.

He has devoted his academic career to studying the Holocaust, antisemitism, mass violence and genocide.

He teaches Holocaust and genocide studies at Stockton University in New Jersey.

He has written extensively about the persecution and mass murder of Jews in Europe, including a book examining the destruction of Jewish communities in the Carpathian region during the Second World War.

In other words, genocide is not a subject he discovered when Israel began bombing Gaza.

It is his life's work.

On October 13, 2023, just six days after the Hamas attacks on Israel, Segal published an article in Jewish Currents.

Its title was direct.

A Textbook Case of Genocide.

He argued that Israel's assault on Gaza was already displaying the characteristics of genocide.

His argument rested on the 1948 Genocide Convention, the siege imposed on Gaza, attacks on civilians and statements by senior Israeli officials.

He pointed particularly to Israeli Defence Minister Yoav Gallant's announcement of a complete siege, cutting off food, electricity and fuel, and his description of the enemy as "human animals."

Segal argued that such declarations were evidence of genocidal intent.

This was October 2023.

He was making that argument before much of the subsequent destruction, displacement and mass death in Gaza.

His conclusion was controversial, even among fellow Holocaust scholars.

But it was a professional assessment grounded in the field to which he had dedicated his life.

Eight months later, Segal was offered one of the most prestigious positions of his career.

The University of Minnesota selected him to become director of its Center for Holocaust and Genocide Studies.

The appointment also included a tenured position in the university's history department.

The selection followed a rigorous academic search and a near-unanimous recommendation by the hiring committee.

Then the objections began.

Two members of the center's advisory board resigned in protest.

Jewish community organizations mobilized against his appointment.

The Jewish Community Relations Council of Minnesota and the Dakotas argued that his position on Israel made him unsuitable to lead a Holocaust studies center.

The university reversed course.

On June 10, 2024, just five days after selecting him, it withdrew the offer.

The man it had chosen to lead its Center for Holocaust and Genocide Studies had become unacceptable after publicly identifying what he considered another genocide.

Segal did not quietly accept the decision.

Represented by the Center for Constitutional Rights, he challenged the university's actions and sought access to internal records.

The controversy raised a question far larger than his individual career.

What happens to academic freedom when a scholar's professional conclusions offend politically influential donors and organizations?

And what is the purpose of genocide studies if scholars risk losing their jobs for applying their knowledge to events unfolding in the present?

The university's critics of Segal maintained that his characterization of Israel's actions was premature, politically extreme and incompatible with the leadership of a Holocaust studies center.

Segal and his supporters argued that a university committed to academic freedom had punished a qualified scholar for expressing a legitimate professional judgment.

Then, in August 2026, came an extraordinary development.

The University of Minnesota agreed to pay Raz Segal $250,000 in a settlement over the withdrawn appointment.

Internal university records obtained by the Center for Constitutional Rights revealed pressure from donors and outside organizations opposed to Segal's criticism of Israel.

The payment did not give him the job back.

Nor did it amount to a court ruling that the university had violated his constitutional rights.

But it represented a significant outcome for a scholar who had challenged the consequences of speaking out.

There is something particularly revealing about this case.

Segal is Jewish.

He is Israeli.

All four of his grandparents survived the Holocaust.

He has spent his professional life researching the destruction of European Jewish communities.

He was qualified enough to be selected to lead a university center devoted to studying genocide.

Yet his assessment of Israel's conduct toward Palestinians helped cost him that very position.

He was not dismissed for denying the Holocaust.

He was not accused of falsifying historical evidence.

His appointment was withdrawn after he applied his understanding of genocide to the actions of the Israeli state.

And when the university finally paid him $250,000 in 2026, it did not reverse the appointment.

It paid to settle the dispute.

Raz Segal's case exposes a troubling contradiction.

Universities encourage scholars to study the historical warning signs of genocide.

But what happens when those scholars recognize such warning signs in an ally of their own government?

For Raz Segal, the answer was the loss of a prestigious job offer.

And, two years later, a $250,000 settlement.
