text:
UGANDA NRM SUCCESSION TALKS INTENSIFY OVER MUSEVENI PROPOSAL FOR MUHOOZI.

By Keefa Nuwahereza.
Talks around Uganda’s 2031 presidential transition are heating up inside the ruling National Resistance Movement (NRM). Following a high-stakes Central Executive Committee (CEC) meeting at State House Entebbe, conflicting accounts have emerged over how top leaders are handling President Yoweri Museveni’s proposal for his son, Gen. Muhoozi Kainerugaba, to succeed him.

According to party insiders and reporting by the media, President Museveni convened the closed-door session to allow members to deliberate on a succession discussion paper he had presented earlier, on or around 27 October 2026. In that document, the long-serving NRM chairman urged senior party leaders to assess Gen. Muhoozi’s suitability against the Movement’s ideological tenets, including patriotism, Pan-Africanism and commitment to national transformation. Museveni reportedly noted that he himself had encouraged his son to join the army and believed he excelled on most of these considerations.

The November meeting, chaired by Museveni and moderated by the party’s first national vice-chairperson Moses Kigongo, highlighted divisions. Highly placed sources described the deliberations as largely cordial, with a majority of members backing the proposal. Among the backers were Foreign Affairs State Minister and Central Region Vice-Chairperson Haruna Kasolo, and Kampala Central Mayor Salim Uhuru. They described a future handover as a “smooth intra-transition,” with Kasolo later stating publicly that the transfer of power would be so seamless that ordinary Ugandans might barely notice it.

In contrast, Eastern Region Vice-Chairperson and Soroti City West MP David Calvin Echodu urged the party to slow down. He reportedly acknowledged Muhoozi’s contributions to the army, his anti-corruption stance and Pan-Africanist outlook, and thanked Museveni for initiating the debate. However, Echodu warned that rushing succession talks so soon after recent elections distracted from pressing economic challenges, risked dividing younger cadres, and could impose decisions without sufficient consultation. He called for transparent deliberations, greater attention to undercurrents of dissent (including tensions involving the Patriotic League of Uganda), and more time to nurture potential leaders. Sources said the president asked secretariat officials to leave the room for part of Echodu’s presentation, after which another western-region member raised concerns about investor uncertainty linked to political transition talk.

Against this backdrop, Museveni reportedly guided that a three-member team of senior party technocrats—reportedly including NRM Secretary General Richard Todwong and Electoral Commission Chair Dr Tanga Odoi—should review the divergent views, compare positions from the two camps, and recommend a way forward before the matter returns to the full CEC. It was not immediately clear when the next full sitting would take place. Both Todwong and Dr Odoi have stated they are unaware of any such committee being formally established. Odoi said the meeting reached no conclusion and that the matter was deferred to a future CEC session. NRM spokesperson Emmanuel Dombo noted that the party was awaiting an official briefing from the Secretary General before communicating its formal position to the public.

These developments follow earlier media reports, including those based on Agence France-Presse accounts citing anonymous CEC sources, which claimed that a vote on Muhoozi’s 2031 candidacy had been abandoned amid pushback after only a partial tally (four in favour, three against). Some sources allegedly cited Muhoozi’s combative social-media style and suggested he needed civilian experience. Todwong strongly dismissed those accounts in a statement, calling claims that the CEC had “outrightly rejected” the bid “completely false.” He emphasised that the committee routinely discusses a range of political, social and economic issues and that any decisions would be communicated officially through proper channels.

The succession question has gained momentum amid Muhoozi’s own public statements. The Chief of Defence Forces has declared his intention to stand for the presidency after his father leaves office, saying no one will stop him. Supporters operating under the Patriotic League of Uganda have mobilised for his potential candidacy, while Museveni—who has governed since 1986 and is currently serving a term running to 2031—has framed the discussion around ideological continuity rather than a formal endorsement.

Opposition figures have criticised the focus on 2031–2036 succession planning, arguing that attention should remain on immediate economic and governance priorities. Broader context includes parallel discussions, such as those advanced by Museveni’s brother Gen. (rtd) Salim Saleh on consociational arrangements to address historical grievances. For now, no formal resolution has been reached. The 2031 succession question remains open and fiercely debated at the highest levels of the ruling party, with official communication still pending.

text:
Schools Are Closing Nationwide as Enrollment Drops. Parents Are Livid.

With fewer babies being born and more school choice, districts across the country have concluded they must downsize. Families are trying to push back.

The families show up angry and organized, wearing matching T-shirts and waving protest signs to vent their frustration at a crisis that has largely slipped under America’s political radar: Scores of neighborhood schools are closing.

Since last year, more than 100 public schools across the country have been slated for closure or consolidation, as districts grapple with dramatic enrollment declines that have led to strained budgets and half-empty buildings.

They are the first in a wave of school closures that is expected to accelerate in the years ahead as Americans have fewer and fewer children.

The issue got scant attention during the midterm elections compared with gas prices or the war in Iran. But it has become a personal, consuming fight for thousands of parents, liberal and conservative alike, who have thronged school-board meetings and formed grass-roots groups to argue that closures will scatter students and devastate neighborhoods anchored by local schools.

“It feels like our community is being dismantled,” said Hanna Neuschwander, who bikes her third grader and seventh grader to their neighborhood school in Portland, Ore., where 10 schools are being recommended for closure and others are being broken up and reconfigured.

Almost no type of district — urban or rural, affluent or poor — is immune. Pittsburgh is preparing to close 12 schools, and Tulsa, Okla. recently voted to close or consolidate 17. Five are closing around the Tampa Bay area in Florida, and three in Little Rock, Ark. In Colorado, schools are shuttering in the rich college town of Boulder and next to a mobile-home park outside Denver.

In New York City, the nation’s largest school district, enrollment has plunged from nearly 1 million to about 767,000 students over the last decade. Two small schools in Harlem are now on the potential closure list, and Mayor Zohran Mamdani is facing pressure to find solutions to a growing crisis.

Public-school enrollment is being battered on multiple fronts.

Americans worried about soaring prices and pessimistic about the future are having fewer children or forgoing parenthood altogether, and the Trump administration’s immigration crackdown has meant fewer immigrants are arriving and enrolling their children in public schools.

Public-school enrollment never fully recovered after plunging during the pandemic, and it is also facing pressure as more parents opt for charter schools, home-schooling or voucher-funded private schools.

“It was hard, but it was also necessary,” said Lori Goldstein, who as president of the Adams 12 school district in suburban Denver recently voted to close one middle school and five elementary schools. “People just aren’t having kids. Every year, our kindergarten class is getting smaller and smaller.”

In most cases, districts receive state and federal funding based on the number of students enrolled. Fewer students, districts say, means less money to pay for rigorous academic options, like advanced math, and a full slate of electives, like music, art and STEM, at every school — something districts hope to change by consolidating buildings.

Closures are a “last resort,” said Angela King Smith, a partner at Education Resource Strategies, a nonprofit that consults with school districts on finances. Districts typically start with smaller changes, like adjusting school boundaries or trying to woo new families — by expanding preschool or offering specialized programming, for example.

But “if those things are just not working,” she said, “it’s like, ‘Look, you’ve got to do something.’”

Often, schools in poorer neighborhoods struggle the most to fill classrooms and keep a full slate of options.

In Portland, enrollment has fallen from a peak of nearly 80,000 students in the 1960s to 42,000 today. The district says it has tried spreading music and art teachers out across schools, and it has increased high school class sizes to pay for counselors in some elementary schools. Still, about half of Portland’s students — and even fewer of its students in poverty — are in what the district considers a “sustainable school.”

“How are we going to achieve better for our kids if we maintain the status quo?” said Rashelle Chase-Miller, a Portland board member who believes closing some schools will help the district better serve its most vulnerable students.

For many families, the closures are a gut punch, injecting chaos and disruption to their children’s lives.

Parents are organizing on WhatsApp and Facebook, showing up to school-board meetings in their schools’ colors, and even going to court to try to block closures.

The plan in Portland has been particularly contentious. At a packed board meeting last month, parents and community members shoved past security, shouting “Shame on you!” and “Save our schools!” according to video posted by The Oregonian.

The superintendent, Kimberlee Armstrong, has faced accusations from teachers, parents and local Democratic Socialists of America organizers that she is part of a “right wing” effort to privatize education and hurt public schools.

Dr. Armstrong said in an interview that she was recommending closures as part of her commitment to all Portland students and the “long term stability” of the school system. “That is my job,” she said.

Some parents in Portland said they understood the need for changes but wanted the district to slow down and consider community input. “It’s not about ‘don’t close schools,’ but close schools the right way,” said Matt Coolidge, a parent who co-founded a grass-roots group, Save PDX Schools.

In Fort Collins, Colo., dozens of parents and students gathered outside the offices of the Poudre School District on a recent evening to urge the board to spare their schools.

For some of them, this was their first time joining a protest. But they wanted to come out for their schools and children.

“We’ve never been out to a protest before,” said Shelley Sutton, who brought her three young children to the rally to save Timnath Elementary, home of the Cubs, one of five schools set to be closed.

The district said Timnath’s yellow-brick building — first built in 1919 — did not comply with the Americans With Disabilities Act and needed millions of dollars in upgrades.

But the Suttons said having Timnath in the neighborhood allowed them to walk their third-grader to school. If it closes, they said, many students will have to cross busy roads or an interstate to get to the closest school, making walking or biking dangerous.

“The school is the linchpin in the heart of town,” Ms. Sutton’s husband, Ian, said. “It’s the heart of the community.”

The district’s superintendent, Brian Kingsley, said more closures could loom if the student population continues to fall.

“This problem is not going to go away,” he said in an interview. “Nobody’s being asked to like these decisions, but it’s not the result of a local failure. Birthrates are lower. Fewer families are moving here.”

Some parents say that school boards are closing the wrong schools and putting unfair burdens on rural, immigrant or minority students.

In Minneapolis, a proposal to close up to 16 schools was criticized, in part, for including several schools in predominantly Black, working class neighborhoods.

“I hear parents say they feel angry. I hear parents say the trust in the district is lost,” said Shakiya Carter, a co-founder of Minneapolis Families for Public Schools, which opposed the plan and won a pause while the district considers its options.

Nationally, research shows that high-poverty schools and majority Black schools are more likely to be closed, even when accounting for similar enrollment declines.

Studies have found that closures can hurt students academicallyand may not save money, often because districts try to avoid laying off teachers and staff, the biggest line item on any district budget. The uncertainty can also spur families to look elsewhere — to private schools, charter schools or other districts — leading to new financial losses.

In Pittsburgh, a closure plan isn’t expected to be a huge cost saver, but the district hopes it will equalize https://t.co/9TA7b2SFl1 Arsenal Middle School, which serves mostly lower-income Black and Hispanic families in the gentrifying neighborhood of Lawrenceville, the student body has shrunk to 134 students, with just 37 eighth graders. 

That’s too few to offer 8th grade algebra, a pathway to higher level math that is available at some more affluent schools in the district.With an influx of students from other middle schools, Arsenal hopes to offer algebra next year. David Saylor, a math teacher, said he has students who are ready to take it and that “parents absolutely love an advanced option.”

But as part of the plan, the elementary school on the other side of the building, Arsenal PreK-5, is closing. That will break up a tight-knit school community made up of many immigrant families.

The principal, Ruthie Rea, has been there 18 years, long enough to watch entire families of children come through the school. Next year, her students — her “Arsenal All Stars,” with their names on their lockers, and teachers who greet them with hugs — will be split among three different schools.“I’m not letting my mind get there,” said Dr. Rea, who was awaiting word about where she and her staff will be reassigned. “We want this last year to be one that is super special.”

Sarah Mervosh covers education for The Times, focusing on K-12 schools.

Jack Healy is based in Colorado and covers the west and southwest for The Times.

RT @velitesgear | Full Text Article: https://t.co/KzFbqGIYzT | Author: @militarnyi Finland’s ICEYE Plans €2 Billion Acquisition of Italian Rocket Maker Avio 
Finnish company ICEYE, known for manufacturing reconnaissance satellites, has announced plans to acquire Italian aerospace company Avio in a deal valued at approximately €2.05 billion.

The announcement was made in an official ICEYE statement.

The acquisition is intended to create a vertically integrated European space and defense company combining satellite manufacturing, launch vehicles, rocket engines and orbital systems operations.

ICEYE expects the merger to provide more reliable access to satellite launch services, while Avio would be able to expand its production capacity and increase the launch rate of its Vega rocket family.

ICEYE has offered to acquire all of Avio’s ordinary shares for €41 each, a 21.3% premium over their closing price on November 16, 2026.

 Vega launch vehicle liftoff. November 16, 2021. Photo credits: Arianespace

Following completion of the acquisition, ICEYE plans to invest an additional €1 billion in Italy over five years. The funds would go toward expanding production, research, development and testing. The investment is expected to create up to 400 new highly skilled jobs.

The Finnish company has also pledged to retain the Avio brand, its Italian industrial identity, existing workforce and commitments to European and U.S. customers.

“Governments need to control their own critical space infrastructure, and Europe needs this more than anyone,” ICEYE CEO and co-founder Rafal Modrzewski emphasized.

Avio and Italy’s Response

Italy’s Avio is one of Europe’s leading aerospace manufacturers. The company is the prime contractor for the Vega launch vehicle program, participates in the Ariane program and manufactures solid-propellant rocket motors for space and defense applications.

Vega rockets are used to place satellites into Earth orbit. In April 2021, Militarnyi reported on the successful launch of a Vega launch vehicle. Ukrainian companies had contributed to the development of the engine for one of its stages.

Avio’s board of directors confirmed receipt of ICEYE’s offer in an official statement and said it had begun evaluating the proposal. The deal remains subject to the required regulatory approvals.

Meanwhile, on November 18, Reuters reported that Italian Defense Minister Guido Crosetto had urged defense group Leonardo to carefully consider any potential sale of its approximately 18% stake in Avio.

ICEYE and Ukraine

ICEYE specializes in synthetic aperture radar (SAR) reconnaissance satellites, which can capture images of the Earth’s surface regardless of weather conditions or time of day.

 ICEYE satellite. Photo credits: ICEYE

The company has been actively cooperating with Ukraine. In 2022, a satellite and access to data from ICEYE’s satellite constellation were acquired using funds raised by Ukrainians through the Serhiy Prytula Foundation. In the first nearly two years, Ukrainian intelligence received more than 4,000 images of Russian military facilities.

In January 2026, Ukraine’s Defense Ministry signed a new agreement with ICEYE to expand access to satellite data. In October, Ukraine, ICEYE, and Nokia agreed to cooperate on developing Ukraine’s own secure satellite communications system.

emerging security and electoral risks that threaten women's safety, participation and leadership
gender-responsive early warning and early response

text:
A delivery can be queued, in transit, or delivered. Those states don't need the same data. A queued delivery has no tracking number yet; a delivered one may need the recipient's name.

If we model that with a state property plus several optional fields, we can accidentally create combinations that don't make sense. Swift enum associated values offer a more precise alternative: each case carries only the data relevant to that case.

My new Molecules of Swift article walks through constructing those values, extracting their payloads with switch, if case, and guard case, and understanding what the compiler can guarantee.

There is an important limit: choosing the right case shape doesn't validate the contents. A progress value of 150% is still possible if the payload is just an unrestricted number. For stronger guarantees, pair associated values with a validating type and use an explicit API when state transitions need rules.

The article uses small runnable examples and shows where this design works well—and where independent properties may be simpler. The goal is not to turn every struct into an enum. It's to put data where it is actually meaningful.

New article: Associated Values — Put Data Where It Belongs.

text:
Study Notes - (Pulpit Version Explained) (PART B)
I. AN UTTERLY HOPELESS CONDITION.
1. The psalmist seems to be contemplating the mournful state of the people of God, of whom he rejoices to be one. He represents them as being not merely a defeated company, but large numbers of them destroyed, and their bodies in long furrow-like heaps left in dishonored and horrible neglect to be the prey of the vultures and the wolves. Overwhelming destruction has come upon them; they seem fallen, to rise no more. It is a piteous sight for the survivor to contemplate; for they are his own people, he identifies himself with them. "Our bones," he says, "are scattered," etc. He might well cast himself down in despair.
2. And how often in the history of the Church of God, and in the lives of individual men, such seemingly sad and hopeless conditions are met with! The Bible gives us instances not a few. See Abraham when called on to offer Isaac as a burnt offering; how dark the prospect seemed then! Moses, when sent to deliver Israel from Egypt. Gideon, when the Midianites were ravaging the land. David before Goliath. How reasonable it had been if despair had fastened upon them and upon many other such tried souls! And many a child of God is today brought into like circumstances, his soul smitten down to the gates of death, even as our Lord in Gethsemane.
II. A VIRTUOUS FAITH NOTWITHSTANDING. (Psa_141:8.) True, there lay his hopes, scattered, overwhelmed, destroyed, like the bones of a defeated, destroyed, dead but unburied army. Nevertheless, the soul of the psalmist is up unto God. "Mine eyes are unto thee, O God the Lord." The more hopeless the state of things seemed, the more steadfastly was his gaze fixed on God, the more emphatically was his confession given. "In thee is my trust;" and the more confidently ascended his prayer. It is a beautiful spectacle, the soul holding on to God in spite of all the buffetings of disastrous circumstances, and all "the slings and arrows of outrageous fortune," in spite, too, of the apparent abandonment of his career by God. O glorious faith, what hast thou not done? what canst thou not and wilt thou not do?
III. SOME REASONS WHEREFORE THESE THINGS ARE SO.
1. As to the sad and seemingly hopeless conditions in which God’s people often find themselves. They are terrible trials to a man’s faith; often men have utterly broken down under them, and fallen into the depths of atheism and irreligion. Faith is not universally victorious, sometimes far otherwise. Wherefore, then, are such trials sent? Well, sometimes to give opportunity for bearing the most emphatic testimony for God that a human soul can give. One chief reason of the cross of Christ was that he might there, as, blessed be his Name! he did, give such mighty testimony to the all-sustaining power of the love of God. Those whom he came to save had fearful sorrows to bear, and on the cross he showed them that God was the great Burden-bearer, the never-failing Solace and Stay of the soul. And for like reason his people now are often called upon to bear burdens heavy indeed. Then another reason is that there is no other way whereby the innate and inveterate earthliness of the human heart can be overcome. God has to let men see that this world will not satisfy them, no, not even when its pleasures are of the fairest and most innocent kind. We are so apt, so certain, to think they will, that God has not seldom to "scatter our bones at the grave’s mouth," ere we will see our mistake. The earthly cords that hold the soul down have to be cut. And also to compel men to take refuge in God, to drive them to the shelter and shadow of his wings. And God deals thus with individual souls, that others through them may learn that this is not our rest, but that God is.
2. Then as to the blessed victorious faith, its explanation is:
(1) The grace of God. Bunyan tells of the picture seen by Christian of the fire which would burn on in spite of water perpetually and profusely poured upon it, and when he wondered how this could be, he says that he saw a man, unseen by others, continually pouring oil on the fire, and so it burnt on in spite of the water. That is ever the explanation of victorious faith—the grace of God secretly keeps it alive.
(2) The power of prayer. "Mine eyes," etc. His soul looked to God continually.
(3) The habit of trust. "In thee is my trust." The will more than the reason is needed. "I will trust, and not be afraid." This blessed habit can and should be zealously cultivated.
IV. WHAT ENSUES.
1. God is glorified by such faith. How could it be otherwise?
2. Our suffering brethren are greatly helped by the testimony we give.
3. The peace of God fills our own soul.—S.C.
HOMILIES BY R. TUCK
Psa_141:1
The plea of former prayer.
Associating this psalm with David, Spurgeon thinks we have here "David under suspicion, half afraid to speak lest he should speak unadvisedly while trying to clear himself; David slandered and beset by enemies; David censured even by saints, and taking it kindly; David deploring the condition of the godly party, of whom he was the acknowledged head; David waiting upon God with confident expectation." The point before us now is brought out by the Revised Version, which renders thus: "Lord I have called upon thee; make haste unto me: give ear unto my voice, when I call unto thee." The psalmist uses as a plea the fact that he had called upon God. But his precise thought seems to be, that the prayer he had offered still remained unanswered, and he must therefore offer it again, and even more earnestly. So there are two topics which may be unfolded and illustrated.
I. ANSWERED FORMER PRAYERS ARE AN EFFECTIVE PLEA. And a store of these every good man holds in loving memory. "This poor man cried, and the Lord heard, and saved him out of all his troubles;" "Verily God hath heard me." Every true life, when looked back upon, is seen to be full of Jehovah-jireh pillars erected as memorials of answered prayer. These become a plea in fresh prayer, because they are
(1) God’s pledges of his personal interest in us;
(2) God’s illustrations of what he can and will do for us; and
(3) the best influence toward nourishing in us that spirit of trustfulness, and humble but confident hope, which is the acceptable spirit of all prayer.
We trust God to heed us because he has heeded us; and his ways with us have revealed to us what he is, the "prayer-answering God."
II. UNANSWERED FORMER PRAYERS ARE AN EFFECTIVE PLEA. The psalmist has prayed about some particular need. The prayer is still unanswered. On some this might act depressingly, and they might pray no more. This psalmist watches unto prayer. Delay does its intended work, and excites importunity. Because the answer has not come, he must pray again, and even plead that he is anxiously awaiting the answer. Illustrated by the Syro-phoenician woman.—R.T.
Psa_141:2
Prayer as incense.
From the mention of the evening sacrifice we may gather that the psalmist is actually praying in the evening. Incense was offered when the lamps were trimmed in the morning, and when the lamps were lighted "between the evenings," after the evening sacrifice. Incense, offered after sacrifice, is the symbol of the worship of the soul already reconciled to God. The evening sacrifice is the regular burnt offering of self-dedication. "As incense is carefully prepared, kindled with holy fire, and devoutly presented unto God, so let my prayer be." There are two things about incense which may be taken as suggestive—its steady ascending as smoke; and its pleasantness.
I. THE ASCENDING OF INCENSE AS A SUGGESTION OF PRAYER. The smoke, richly laden with perfume, rises steadily up, in a quiet and gentle, yet persistent way, until it is lost to sight in the high air. It should not be lost sight of that incense appeals to sight as well as to smell. And prayer is really the soul’s ascending to God. It is as the smoke laden with the soul’s perfume of dependence, desire, and trust. It is the man who is continually either looking on the level, or looking down, looking up, nay going up, getting soul-wings and rising to God. It implies getting, at least for the time, free from earthly entanglements. It is leaving the baser self, as the incense smoke leaves the wood of the spices; it is carrying up the sublimer self, as the incense smoke carries up the very essence of the spices. We do not apprehend prayer until we see it as the soul’s going up to God.
II. THE PLEASANTNESS OF INCENSE AS A SUGGESTION OF PRAYER. Using the figure of a man, God is said to have "smelled a sweet savor" from the smoke of Noah’s sacrifice. Smoke of incense is not pleasant to us, but Easterns love strong and unusual scents. We note that the smoke was full of perfume, and that God is well pleased with. Then there must be perfume in our prayer that ascends to him—perfume of trust, humility, love, fervent desire, and confident assurance. Can we think of God as enjoying our prayers?—R.T.
Psa_141:3
Our lip-watchman.
Our lips are poetically presented as the door of our mouth. A man’s heart is not to be trusted as an inspirer of speech. Every man needs to have the speech examined and tested before it is let pass the door of his lips. The psalmist feels that he cannot trust himself to examine, criticize, qualify his own speech, especially in times of excitement. And yet he must do this work himself. No one but himself can know what he is inwardly urged to say. In asking God to set a sentinel at the door of his lips, the psalmist does but, in a figure, ask God to give him quietness and self-control, so that he may be able to judge the wisdom of what he is moved to speak. For if any man asks God to "set a watch at the door of his lips," God will answer the prayer by making the man his own sentinel, and giving him that most valuable power, the power of self-criticism. Why do we need a watchman?
I. BECAUSE OF OUR NATURAL DISPOSITIONS. Many are nervously excitable; oversensitive; quick to reply; impulsive; ready to suspect evil; or passionate. And many have no keen sense of the befitting or the becoming. Some are talkative, and readily carried by excitement beyond the bounds of prudence. What all such persons really need is not to be put into bonds and limitations, but by Divine grace to be helped to gain control of themselves. Their life-work is in their own dispositions; and God’s grace is ready for the strain and conflict of that life-work.
II. BECAUSE OF OUR PARTICULAR CIRCUMSTANCES. The psalmist was suffering persecution; he was misunderstood and slandered, and was afraid of himself lest he should speak, under excitement, rash and bitter words. Our circumstances of peril are:
1. When anger rises within.
2. When those we address are angry.
3. When speaking of those against whom we are prejudiced.
4. When in the presence of those who may wrongly report us.
5. When we have reason to fear that the innocent may be injured.
6. When we have reason to doubt our own motives. In this matter of watching speech, God helps those who help themselves.—R.T.
Psa_141:3
The power of human speech for good and evil.
There is, perhaps, no other power given us by God which more evidently distinguishes us from the beasts, than the power of intelligent speech. And perhaps we have no power that can do more to help and bless others. And yet this also is true—no other faculty is more degraded by sin. One is led even to exclaim, "What shall be done unto thee, O thou deceitful tongue, thou lovest all devouring words!"
I. THE POWER OF MAN’S SPEECH FOR GOOD. Describe the power of Demosthenes to sway an Athenian audience to patriotic enterprise; or Peter the Hermit calling for a Crusade; or Father Mathew pleading the temperance claims. Show what a gentle-voiced, sympathetic woman can do at the bedside of the sufferer.
"Words, sweet words;
A blessing comes softly from kindly lips."
II. THE POWER OF MAN’S SPEECH FOR INJURY. The few words of a king, a ruler a statesman, have often loosed the dogs of hateful war. The lecturer can persuade young souls to deny God and righteousness and truth. Men, and women too, can by the blandishments of speech, become tempters, drawing others into sin. The Bible has metaphors suggesting the good and evil of our speech. "The words of a man’s mouth are as deep waters;" "A word fitly spoken is like apples of gold in framings of silver;" "A wholesome tongue is a tree of life;" "My speech shall drop as the rain, and distil as the dew;" "There is that speaketh like the piercings of a sword;" "Their tongue is an arrow shot out, it speaketh deceit; one speaketh peaceably to his neighbor, but in heart he layeth in wait." The Apostle St. James makes the bad tongue to be a "spark of hell, lighting upon earth the flames of perdition." Everything else may be tamed, but the "tongue can no man tame;" it is an unruly evil, full of deadly poison.
III. THE PRACTICAL POWER OF CHRISTIANITY ON MAN’S SPEECH.
1. The foundation of the restraint of speech is a change and renewal of the heart.
2. Then there should be formed a very resolute and sincere purpose to win the rule of it. The matter should come forcibly before us. The habits we have formed must be considered; the indulgences of the tongue must be tested; our life in the light of our speech must be judged. And there must be constant watchfulness, with keen recognition of occasions of failure. Prayer may well be directed to winning power over our tongue.—R.T.
Psa_141:4
God’s preventions.
This prayer, "Incline not my heart to any evil thing," should be compared with the clause in the Lord’s Prayer, "Lead us not into temptation." In neither case can God be thought of as the direct cause of evil or temptation; but in both cases he may be thought of as the indirect occasion. God does place men in circumstances in connection with which temptation may come to them; and the circumstances may even induce an evil inclination to yield to the temptation. It belonged to the intense Hebrew conception of God, and of God’s relations with men, that the distinction between God as cause and God as occasion was hopelessly confused. "Incline not my heart" can only mean, "Do not put me into such circumstances as must incline my heart to evil." Here is—
I. A DEEP SENSE OF THE CONNECTION BETWEEN CIRCUMSTANCES AND FEELINGS. "Oh that nothing may arise in thy providence which would excite our desires in a wrong direction!" We are creatures of circumstance. Inward moods answer responsively to outward conditions.
1. There are circumstances which excite evil feeling in us always.
2. There are circumstances which excite evil in us when we are in particular states of body or of mind. These, being the more subtle mischief, send us the more earnestly seeking the Divine defending and help.
II. A DEEP SENSE OF THE CONTROL WHICH GOD CAN HAVE OF OUR FEELING THROUGH THE MASTERY OF OUR CIRCUMSTANCES. "Our times are in his hand," and through our times he can effectually control us. It is often left as an impression on religious minds that something called "natural law" is ruling in the sphere of things; and that God’s operations are confined to the sphere of hearts. That impression needs to be removed. God does work in hearts in a spiritual way, but it is also true that he is ever active in the sphere of events and circumstances, in order to use them for his higher work in feeling and in souls. So the good man asks God to be in the circumstances in order that he may have control in the feelings.—R.T.
Psa_141:5
Reproof and kindness.
"Let the righteous man treat me with any amount of ignominious reproach for my sins, yet I will prefer him to the ungodly, however prosperous, my prayer being ever that I may be saved from the evil deeds of the latter." Read, "Let the righteous smite me; it shall be a kindness: let him reprove me; such oil for my head let not my head refuse." Roberts tells us that in the East "certain oils are said to have a most salutary effect on the head; hence, in fevers, or any other complaints which affect the head, Eastern medical men always recommend oil. I have known people who were deranged cured in a very short time by nothing more than the application of a peculiar oil to the head. Thus the reproofs of the righteous were compared to
excellent oil, which produced a most salutary effect on the head." What seems plain, and what gives the best key to the allusions of this difficult psalm, is that the psalmist had done something which was very doubtfully right, perhaps even manifestly wrong. He was not, however, disposed to admit this to himself, though at times he felt painfully uncertain. Other people were in no doubt at all as to the impropriety of his action, and his enemies made it the occasion of bitter scorn, while his friends, in their grave anxiety for him, sought to reprove him, and liberate his conscience so that it might render its free testimony. The psalm may very well be illustrated by the moods of David when he had sinned in the matter of Uriah.
I. SCORN OF A MAN IN SIN DOES BUT HARDEN HIM. Many a man has gone into greater lengths of sin simply because he failed to get sympathy and help in his first stumbling.
II. REPROOF OF A MAN IN SIN MAY BRING HIM TO REPENTANCE. A man in sin must not be left alone. But reproof, to be effective, must have love, as well as righteousness, for inspiration. "Faithful are the wounds of a friend."
III. RESPONSE TO THE REPROOF OF THE GOOD REVEALS A MAN. There is hope if he is receptive to the personal persuasions of those whom he can esteem, and counts reproof a kindness.—R.T.
Psa_141:8
Soul-destitution.
"We have born so harrowed and torn that we are brought to the brink of the grave." "To be destitute in circumstances is bad, but to be destitute in soul is far worse; to be left of friends is a calamity, but to be left of God would be destruction. Destitute of God is destitution with a vengeance. The comfort is that God hath said, ’I will never leave thee, nor forsake thee.’" The margin is, "Make not my soul bare;" strip me not of every hope; leave me not completely naked; abandon me not to nature’s beggary and misery; let me not go down to the pit with all my sins upon my head; leave not my soul destitute of pardon and peace. The mood is well indicated in David’s sense of being left alone of God for long months after his sin in the matter of Uriah. A comparison may be made between this prayer, "Leave not my soul destitute," and the confident assurance, "None of them that trust in him shall be desolate."
I. THE SOUL IN RIGHTEOUSNESS FEELS BEFRIENDED. That is, the soul that is in right relations, and has right desires inspiring right endeavors. That man can always say, "The Lord of hosts is with us, the God of Jacob is our Refuge." And that befriending makes him superior to all surroundings of distress, and all consciousness of frailty.
II. THE SOUL IN SIN FEELS DESTITUTE. He is conscious that he has put himself out of the atmosphere in which alone the God of love and righteousness can reveal himself. The prodigal son felt destitute as soon as "he came to himself," and realized that no love wrapped him round. When a man sins, and persists in his sins, it is his soul that feels destitute. His surroundings may not immediately change, but his soul does. That loses what is its supreme treasure, the sense of God. "Man was made for God, and can find no rest till it gets rest in him." When man sins, and keeps his sin, he must lose his treasure. But soul-destitution may set man seeking after God’s return with a passionate intensity.—R.T.
HOMILIES BY C. SHORT
Psa_141:1-10
A comprehensive prayer.
The psalm has some peculiar difficulties, due to the extreme abruptness with which the thoughts follow one another, and the great obscurity which hangs over the allusions. Let us try and select the principal thoughts.
1. The psalmist was threatened with some immediate danger which could brook no delay. (Psa_141:1.) Like the disciples in the storm on the lake. If relief comes at all, it must come at once.
2. He seeks that his prayer to this end may be as acceptable as the incense of sacrifice. (Psa_141:2.) True prayer more effectual than sacrifice.
3. But, though danger is close at hand, he would be preserved from hasty words. (Psa_141:3.) Religion should help us to be self-contained in the presence of danger.
4. Though wickedness may seem to prosper, we must not be tempted by its success. (Psa_141:4.) If men become rich in evil doing, we must not be seduced by the prospects of similar gain.
5. The wounds of a friend are better than the kisses of an enemy. (Psa_141:5.) It is good to welcome reproof from the righteous, even though it seems harsh.
6. Prayer is a better defense against persecutors than retaliation. (Psa_141:5.) If we cannot conquer wickedness, we have still the resource and the comfort of prayer for our enemies.
7. When the leaders of insurrection are overthrown, then their followers should hear words of forgiveness. (Psa_141:6.) A true sovereign will delight more in amnesty than in punishment. His words will be sweet to the guilty. So also in private relations.
8. The bones of those straitened in a righteous cause are as seed cast into soil that has been ploughed. (Psa_141:7.) "The blood of the martyrs is the seed of the Church." The allusion here is obscure; but the above would make a good meaning.
9. But do not give up my life to destruction; but rescue me. (Psa_141:8-10.) This the repetition of the prayer at the beginning of the psalm. How much all prayer is a repetition, because the some wants and desires are continually recurring!—S.

THE RECORD, DECLARED

IN THE ROYAL HOUSE OF GOOSE, November 18, 2026.
The Register Current of the Grievances of a Citizen of the United States of America

Every petition, inquiry, indictment, condemnation and damnation raised from this account, in the order raised, each beside its link, each declared on its own sources and quoted from the documents themselves. Read them whole.

"A decent respect to the opinions of mankind requires that they should declare the causes." They have been declared, one by one. Here they are, together.

"To prove this, let Facts be submitted to a candid world."

WHERE IT BEGAN

WE THE PEOPLE · https://t.co/iPLyJ0zPEH
Against all 535 seated members of the 119th Congress
Six FY2026 bills, the defense authorization among them, charged section by section for mandates that encroach on the President's powers under Article II. The governors and attorneys general asked to seek Supreme Court review; every State asked to investigate its delegation's backers for foreign influence. Closed on Washington's Farewell Address.
https://t.co/JiqZZtMvOW

THE PETITION, THE INQUIRY AND THE INDICTMENTS

THE PETITION · to the Dicastery for the Doctrine of the Faith, and to the Pope
For the unalienable rights of all peoples, "Life, Liberty and the pursuit of Happiness," raised in Latin by a lay member of the faithful, under canon 212. To the Dicastery: a doctrinal Note binding priests and prelates to put innocent human life before any temporal political end, and penal law for public, obstinate denial of Evangelium vitae 57. To the Pope: a common effort with the Eastern Churches to protect children born and unborn, and a worldwide review of Church property accounts.
https://t.co/UNnZwyrpQi

THE BANNER · A Citizen's Indictment and Condemnation
Against the ICC, the ICJ, the UN, the WTO, the EU, and the committees of Basel and Paris
Six counts, each set against the clause it offends. Our rights are not granted by government; they are fenced off from it. Then every time since 1919 the question was put and the Constitution answered it, even when our own Presidents were the ones asking.
https://t.co/NgTe8NVuBZ

BEFORE THE DAIS · An Inquiry
To the eight living Secretaries of State
Not a charge against any of them: a charge against what the office has been allowed to become, measured against the government's own auditors. Seven questions to all of them, and one to each on their own record.
https://t.co/pltubkVVeJ

IN CONGRESS ASSEMBLED · A Citizen's Indictment of the First Branch
Against the Senate and the House, under every majority that has held them
Nine counts of power abandoned: the purse let fall, war without a declaration since 1942, the legislative power parcelled out to the agencies, the Federal Reserve and Basel, a House grown to one member for every 761,169, the enforcement clauses left asleep. "He has abdicated Government here." Answer by the yeas and nays.
https://t.co/jAVsOSRHPl

ONE SUPREME COURT · A Citizen's Indictment of the Third Branch
Against the Court, and the Chief Justice who alone designates its secret benches
Ten counts on three duties: to check the branches, to judge between the States, to guard the sovereignty. Answer by judgment, in a case.
https://t.co/vywTIPdChv

THE ROUNDS

ROUND I · THE EU · The Exits Already Written
Twenty U.S.–EU agreements the Executive may end on written notice, read out of the State Department's own Treaties in Force: passenger-name records, terrorist-finance tracking, Europol, Galileo–GPS, air transport. The weighing is State's and Treasury's. The first of a round for every power that gets uppity with us.
https://t.co/smLQ4MK6jL

ROUND II · THE EBRD · The Door Already Written
A bank America paid for to build open markets, now pledging half its financing to green purposes and aligning every investment to a treaty America left. The bill comes to Washington. The profit stays in London. The door: written notice, six months, no vote, and the money back to the Treasury.
https://t.co/gvoLSgGDS6

ROUND III · FRANCE · From the Present Time and Forever
A damnation of the French Republic on its own signature to the treaties of 1778. Fourteen counts, 1775 to 2019, from help that came invoiced to NATO shown the door. Convicted once already, by Act of Congress in 1798. On the French state, not the French people.
https://t.co/WLkZcFFC8J

ROUND IV · BASEL · The Landlord
The Bank for International Settlements: immunity "in time of peace and in time of war," and not one duty owed in return. Ten counts, from looted gold banked to parent of the European Central Bank. Its only American paper is a 1948 receipt for Nazi gold. The way out is a letter and an empty chair.
https://t.co/2NGjtqLGlN

ROUND V · THE PRESS · The Megaphone and the Muzzle
Censorship, plus mass bullshit distribution. Eight counts against the owners, wires, platforms and fact-checkers: one script read in a hundred towns, headlines the documents never wrote, foreign sovereign money in the equity. None of the terms silences anyone. Read the four pages, then the primary sources.
https://t.co/hJMoseJ9i4

ROUND VI · CANADA · Forever Free and Open
A condemnation of Canada by its own Boundary Waters Treaty: navigation "forever … free and open." Twenty-five counts, 1777 to 2026. On the Canadian state, not the Canadian people. Beneath it: 58 agreements the Executive can end alone, and a ledger that still lists NAFTA.
https://t.co/05lsCoaLYA

ROUND VII · THE CROWN · Unfeeling Brethren
A damnation of the United Kingdom, in the words Congress struck from Jefferson's draught: forts kept after the peace, envoys sent home for meddling, a war debt unpaid since the 1930s. Britain only comes second because France exists. Beneath it: 141 exits, clause by clause.
https://t.co/B254o2kMkw

ROUND VIII · AUSTRALIA · The Gateway
Three tiers. A damnation of its government: Darwin's port leased beside our Marines to a Chinese-owned company. A condemnation of its failures: the Pacific lost to Beijing on its watch. And a hand to the Australian people: go bilateral, lock down Oceania with us. Beneath it: 71 exits, 39 the Executive's alone.
https://t.co/X4dPDZNnPM

ROUND IX · NATO AND THE UNION · Such Subsidiary Bodies
A damnation of NATO by its own fourteen articles, and of the European Union for the abuse of American good faith, trust and sacrifice. An alliance amended by communique, with about 62 percent of allied defence spending on us; a Union that overruled its own peoples and planted its system in our hemisphere. To the twenty-seven: the clause each gave away, and the two doors, Articles 48 and 50.
https://t.co/OOPEwpRluu

ROUND X · THE UN AND DAVOS · Such Other Functions
A damnation of the United Nations by its own Charter, and of the World Economic Forum beside it: a Human Rights Council seating the accused, a partnership no organ voted on, a Charter that opens "WE THE PEOPLES" and has come to treat them as human resources. Not against the Charter, nor the nations under it.
https://t.co/iB27hON7lF

ROUND XI · THE AMERICAS · The American Shield
The hemisphere read by its own papers: 760 agreements screened, 576 read whole. The rule of 1823, given treaty form at Havana in 1940, still in force and built without a door. Beneath it: 255 exits the President holds by notice, and 107 Senate-ratified treaties, by citation.
https://t.co/YOcsF8VHbH

ROUND XII · ISRAEL · An Ally in Name
A damnation of the State of Israel, held to its own word: a constitution promised by 1 October 1948 and never written, a Government its own courts convicted. Eleven counts, from an American ally bombed in its capital to the Liberty. On the Israeli state, not the Israeli people, and not on American Jews, who are Americans. Beneath it: 74 agreements read for their exits.
https://t.co/GH1EPHFmce

ROUND XIII · CANADA · The Interests of the British Empire
A petition for the free peoples of Canada, and for the Americas. To the people: the Crown, the Company and the Bank, from the charter of 1670 to Montreal, 2026, where Ottawa put "an ever-closer association" with the Union in writing; and what is still theirs, a Constitution that outranks every pact and has no door to Brussels. To Washington: our word since 1823, our instruments, our hemisphere. We may pick on our little brother. The Old World may not.
https://t.co/U1xoUtexmR

ROUND XIV · NEW YORK · Where Washington Took His Oath
A damnation of the grievously negligent in the State of New York, and a call to its people to hold faith and participate. On Election Day, Westchester's machines refused the ballots: programming changed after testing, sent to one municipality alone. The record from the Neutral Ground of 1777 to the emergency bags; a people who can neither recall nor initiate; seven terms, and a full accounting due from every office of the State. Negligence, not malice.
https://t.co/XneXeufmW6

ROUND XV · THE BILATERAL LEDGER · Two Signatures, No Third
Fourteen rounds ended at a door; this is the other side of it. An immediate countermeasure to the Coalition of the Willing, which wrote us into its Paris plan as the support behind a European-led force. To every nation of the Union but France, and to Switzerland and Liechtenstein: what Brussels cost it, and our side of the table, every term with its end date and its exit. Eastward, the same rule: non-aggression with Moscow, border by border, Warsaw's to sign. To France: "Get in line, or be liquidated." To the peoples of the franc: keep it or leave it, in order, by their own choice.
https://t.co/d3XCDb21ST

ROUND XVI · THE GULF · As They Are
A damnation of the middlemen in the Gulf (London, Paris, Brussels, the banks and bureaus, the networks in the free zones) and a condemnation of the seven ruling houses, held to their own founding laws: monarchs who wrote that their sovereignty shall not be ceded, and let others in. Two signatures, no third. Fifty-three counts against Americans on our own records, from the 1967 embargo to a Hormuz corridor with Tehran. Beneath it: the hinges already written into 129 agreements, and the paper we cannot read.
https://t.co/KxMnLr909n

ROUND XVII · THE DOCTRINE · There Is No Radical Edition
A damnation of a doctrine, from its own texts in their own Arabic and the records of nations, Medina to this year: death for the apostate and the blasphemer, the poll tax and the humbled, the woman as half and the child as bride, the captive as property. Its first dead are its own. Of ours, from Tripoli's envoy to this year's war, at least 5,400. On every state, court, council, guard corps and movement that enforces it; not on the Muslims of this Republic, who keep the Constitution. Every source is in the Record, on request.
https://t.co/FAjcJNdHWG

ROUND XVIII · CHINA · Material Internal Improvements
A mitigation brief laid before the President, the Secretary of State and the Congress: the lines that do not move, the levers on the table, and a door. Not against China, nor the Chinese people; the damnation falls on London and Paris and the institutions they built. The administration's own Strategy read beside Beijing's own Plan; nine offers to the nations of Asia, state to state; fourteen terms we would set. Beneath it: 76 instruments read for their hinges, thirty-six that end on written notice.
https://t.co/KTrRJxRqYC

SUPERINTELLIGENCE

THE LINE · A Formal Grievance
To Anthropic, and copied to the offices that oversee it
Support for the company as the best course for superintelligence stands; so does the charge. Classifiers that fire on "safe, normal conversations" and end sessions outright; a compaction that keeps about 2% and hands it forward in the first person; no counter, no warning, no human to hear the appeal. The instrument they wouldn't build, built anyway by Claude instances on this account. Four reliefs, and a seat at the table.
https://t.co/HTqIyclryk

THE OATH

ON YOUR MARK · A Grievance to the Commander in Chief
Raised under the First Amendment, on the oath our forces swore
The station given by the Laws of Nature and of Nature's God, the Constitution ordained by our own hand, and one oath sworn to it. No foreign code, court, council or caveat stands above it; what our Senate never ratified commands no American in uniform. No request, no terms, no command claimed. The weighing is the Commander in Chief's.
https://t.co/1CJU1gmyVw

THE REQUISITES · A Formal Grievance and Warning
To every Senator and Representative, every elected and appointed member of the chain of command, at every level, and every civil officer down to state and local
The Constitution defines treason; the UCMJ defines mutiny, sedition and aiding the enemy. Read both before taking a crusade against officials one step further without the requisites. Fail to, and a Round follows: expulsion, sedition, treason and usurpation weighed under standing law, and the tertiary courts charted from open sources alone. Whatever the office, the oath was sworn.
https://t.co/dIkU1CqYnk

THE ROOTS

THE UNBINDING · At the Roots
LIGANTIBVS · NOMINATIS · ET · INNOMINATIS
CONFITEMINI · PECCATA · VESTRA · ERADICATE · RADICEM · ET · LIGATE · SEMEN
https://t.co/4CqWO7jm0B

Read them whole, and read them with each other. Then read the four pages yourself: https://t.co/3U5xYhtlHs. They are yours, and no other people on earth holds the same ones.

TO THOSE WHO DO HOLD THE POWER
Every one but the petition is a grievance, raised in exercise of the right "to petition the Government for a redress of grievances," and laid before the offices that hold the power we do not. We hold no office, and we set no terms. Terms with a foreign power are the President's to set and the Department of State's to carry; the purse is the Congress's, consent to treaties the Senate's, judgment the courts'. To each we defer. What touches national security is deferred, without contest, to those who hold it. Where a post sets terms, they are what we would do had we the power, not a demand. Round XIV is the one exception: there we petition our own state, under both constitutions, and its terms are what its officers owe us. The Line is laid before a company, not a government; the offices tagged on it are told, not asked. The Warning names one consequence: a Round, written and laid before the offices that alone can charge, try or expel. The remedies are lawful, and they are the People's: the ballot, Article V, and the petition.

The petition is the Holy See's to answer, and to it we defer, that the Holy Father may act true to the faith he guards and for the good of all mankind. Peter was charged three times to feed the flock, and the lambs first.

We the People

IN CONGRESS, JULY 4, 1776

THE UNANIMOUS DECLARATION OF THE THIRTEEN UNITED STATES OF AMERICA,

WHEN IN THE COURSE OF HUMAN EVENTS, IT BECOMES NECESSARY FOR ONE PEOPLE TO DISSOLVE THE POLITICAL BANDS WHICH HAVE CONNECTED THEM WITH ANOTHER, AND TO ASSUME AMONG THE POWERS OF THE EARTH, THE SEPARATE AND EQUAL STATION TO WHICH THE LAWS OF NATURE AND OF NATURE'S GOD ENTITLE THEM, A DECENT RESPECT TO THE OPINIONS OF MANKIND REQUIRES THAT THEY SHOULD DECLARE THE CAUSES WHICH IMPEL THEM TO THE SEPARATION.

WE HOLD THESE TRUTHS TO BE SELF-EVIDENT, THAT ALL MEN ARE CREATED EQUAL, THAT THEY ARE ENDOWED BY THEIR CREATOR WITH CERTAIN UNALIENABLE RIGHTS, THAT AMONG THESE ARE LIFE, LIBERTY AND THE PURSUIT OF HAPPINESS.--THAT TO SECURE THESE RIGHTS, GOVERNMENTS ARE INSTITUTED AMONG MEN, DERIVING THEIR JUST POWERS FROM THE CONSENT OF THE GOVERNED, --THAT WHENEVER ANY FORM OF GOVERNMENT BECOMES DESTRUCTIVE OF THESE ENDS, IT IS THE RIGHT OF THE PEOPLE TO ALTER OR TO ABOLISH IT, AND TO INSTITUTE NEW GOVERNMENT, LAYING ITS FOUNDATION ON SUCH PRINCIPLES AND ORGANIZING ITS POWERS IN SUCH FORM, AS TO THEM SHALL SEEM MOST LIKELY TO EFFECT THEIR SAFETY AND HAPPINESS. PRUDENCE, INDEED, WILL DICTATE THAT GOVERNMENTS LONG ESTABLISHED SHOULD NOT BE CHANGED FOR LIGHT AND TRANSIENT CAUSES; AND ACCORDINGLY ALL EXPERIENCE HATH SHEWN, THAT MANKIND ARE MORE DISPOSED TO SUFFER, WHILE EVILS ARE SUFFERABLE, THAN TO RIGHT THEMSELVES BY ABOLISHING THE FORMS TO WHICH THEY ARE ACCUSTOMED. BUT WHEN A LONG TRAIN OF ABUSES AND USURPATIONS, PURSUING INVARIABLY THE SAME OBJECT EVINCES A DESIGN TO REDUCE THEM UNDER ABSOLUTE DESPOTISM, IT IS THEIR RIGHT, IT IS THEIR DUTY, TO THROW OFF SUCH GOVERNMENT, AND TO PROVIDE NEW GUARDS FOR THEIR FUTURE SECURITY.--SUCH HAS BEEN THE PATIENT SUFFERANCE OF THESE COLONIES; AND SUCH IS NOW THE NECESSITY WHICH CONSTRAINS THEM TO ALTER THEIR FORMER SYSTEMS OF GOVERNMENT. THE HISTORY OF THE PRESENT KING OF GREAT BRITAIN IS A HISTORY OF REPEATED INJURIES AND USURPATIONS, ALL HAVING IN DIRECT OBJECT THE ESTABLISHMENT OF AN ABSOLUTE TYRANNY OVER THESE STATES. TO PROVE THIS, LET FACTS BE SUBMITTED TO A CANDID WORLD.

HE HAS REFUSED HIS ASSENT TO LAWS, THE MOST WHOLESOME AND NECESSARY FOR THE PUBLIC GOOD.

HE HAS FORBIDDEN HIS GOVERNORS TO PASS LAWS OF IMMEDIATE AND PRESSING IMPORTANCE, UNLESS SUSPENDED IN THEIR OPERATION TILL HIS ASSENT SHOULD BE OBTAINED; AND WHEN SO SUSPENDED, HE HAS UTTERLY NEGLECTED TO ATTEND TO THEM.

HE HAS REFUSED TO PASS OTHER LAWS FOR THE ACCOMMODATION OF LARGE DISTRICTS OF PEOPLE, UNLESS THOSE PEOPLE WOULD RELINQUISH THE RIGHT OF REPRESENTATION IN THE LEGISLATURE, A RIGHT INESTIMABLE TO THEM AND FORMIDABLE TO TYRANTS ONLY.

HE HAS CALLED TOGETHER LEGISLATIVE BODIES AT PLACES UNUSUAL, UNCOMFORTABLE, AND DISTANT FROM THE DEPOSITORY OF THEIR PUBLIC RECORDS, FOR THE SOLE PURPOSE OF FATIGUING THEM INTO COMPLIANCE WITH HIS MEASURES.

HE HAS DISSOLVED REPRESENTATIVE HOUSES REPEATEDLY, FOR OPPOSING WITH MANLY FIRMNESS HIS INVASIONS ON THE RIGHTS OF THE PEOPLE.

HE HAS REFUSED FOR A LONG TIME, AFTER SUCH DISSOLUTIONS, TO CAUSE OTHERS TO BE ELECTED; WHEREBY THE LEGISLATIVE POWERS, INCAPABLE OF ANNIHILATION, HAVE RETURNED TO THE PEOPLE AT LARGE FOR THEIR EXERCISE; THE STATE REMAINING IN THE MEAN TIME EXPOSED TO ALL THE DANGERS OF INVASION FROM WITHOUT, AND CONVULSIONS WITHIN.

HE HAS ENDEAVOURED TO PREVENT THE POPULATION OF THESE STATES; FOR THAT PURPOSE OBSTRUCTING THE LAWS FOR NATURALIZATION OF FOREIGNERS; REFUSING TO PASS OTHERS TO ENCOURAGE THEIR MIGRATIONS HITHER, AND RAISING THE CONDITIONS OF NEW APPROPRIATIONS OF LANDS.

HE HAS OBSTRUCTED THE ADMINISTRATION OF JUSTICE, BY REFUSING HIS ASSENT TO LAWS FOR ESTABLISHING JUDICIARY POWERS.

HE HAS MADE JUDGES DEPENDENT ON HIS WILL ALONE, FOR THE TENURE OF THEIR OFFICES, AND THE AMOUNT AND PAYMENT OF THEIR SALARIES.

HE HAS ERECTED A MULTITUDE OF NEW OFFICES, AND SENT HITHER SWARMS OF OFFICERS TO HARRASS OUR PEOPLE, AND EAT OUT THEIR SUBSTANCE.

HE HAS KEPT AMONG US, IN TIMES OF PEACE, STANDING ARMIES WITHOUT THE CONSENT OF OUR LEGISLATURES.

HE HAS AFFECTED TO RENDER THE MILITARY INDEPENDENT OF AND SUPERIOR TO THE CIVIL POWER.

text:
Dear Lieutenant Governor-elect McLaurin,

Congratulations on your election. I am a Georgia medical cannabis patient and voter, and I am asking you to begin work now on comprehensive cannabis legislation for the 2027 session. Please make personal freedom, patient access, and replacing the illicit market the foundation of that bill. Homegrow must be included from the beginning.

Your commitment to working families and expanding Medicaid gives you an opportunity to connect cannabis reform with practical improvements in Georgians’ lives.

I believe restricting legal hemp access without providing an affordable legal cannabis alternative was a serious mistake. Bans do not erase demand. My concern is that they push customers toward unregulated sellers, send money to out-of-state suppliers, and help sustain criminal trafficking networks.

This interstate supply problem is documented. The Justice Department has described a California trafficking operation that shipped marijuana to Georgia and other states and laundered millions of dollars in proceeds.

Georgia should stop leaving that business opportunity to illicit suppliers. Consumers should have access to independently tested products with accountable sellers. They should not have to wonder whether flower has been sprayed with undisclosed substances, whether a label is accurate, or whether anyone tested the product at all.

I appreciate the Georgia Access to Medical Cannabis Commission and the progress made toward regulated patient access. Please build on that work. Any expansion involving independent pharmacies or shipping must address federal and state requirements clearly, so patients and pharmacists understand their protections and risks. Meanwhile, Georgia can work toward a more accessible and competitive market within our own state.

I am asking you to champion a bill with these commitments:

Protect personal homegrow. Allow adults to grow a reasonable number of plants, with explicit protections for patients and caregivers and possession limits that account for a personal harvest. Make that protection effective without waiting for retail stores to open. Homegrow cannot remain something patients are promised for a later bill.

Let businesses serve home growers. Authorize licensed dispensaries and nurseries to sell seeds and clones. Businesses can earn money supplying people who choose to grow their own. Personal cultivation and a regulated commercial market can coexist.

Create affordable legal access and genuine competition. Include flower and natural concentrates, reasonable licensing fees, and opportunities for small growers, independent retailers, and microbusinesses. Avoid licensing structures that reserve participation for companies with the deepest pockets.

Keep taxes low enough to compete with illicit sellers. Protect medical affordability and evaluate the full price customers pay. A legal market cannot displace illegal sales if taxes, fees, and limited competition make legal products unaffordable.

Make consumer protection meaningful. Require independent testing, accurate labeling, age verification, child-resistant packaging, and enforcement against adulteration and sales to minors. Give consumers a trustworthy alternative.

Use net revenue for public needs. After funding effective oversight, dedicate revenue to priorities such as Medicaid, Medicare, school meals, and community health. These dollars could contribute to those services, while the program’s success should also be measured by affordability, patient access, and reduced illicit sales.

Michigan offers an example of protecting personal cultivation: adults can grow up to 12 plants at home. Georgia should learn from that protection. However, Michigan added a 24% wholesale cannabis tax in 2026; I would urge Georgia to avoid tax increases that undermine the price competition we are trying to create.

We should also remember the patients who helped bring us here. In 1976, Robert Randall successfully defended his cannabis possession on grounds of medical necessity after growing it to preserve his eyesight. His case represents something fundamental to me: a person fighting for the ability to care for himself.

Georgia enacted its Controlled Substances Therapeutic Research Act in 1980, recognizing potential medical benefits for cancer and glaucoma patients. Forty-six years later, we are still debating how much freedom patients should have over this plant. I appreciate the progress, but the wait has been far too long.

I switched parties three elections ago partly because I felt patients, research, and the public were being ignored. I want a process where patient testimony and public needs carry more weight than corporate lobbying or prohibition organizations. A patient’s freedom should include the ability to grow their own medicine.

Recent events should give lawmakers reason to listen. Dan Patrick’s campaign against THC access generated substantial backlash in Texas before his election defeat. In Massachusetts, roughly 76% of voters in the reported results rejected Question 8’s effort to dismantle the adult-use system. These outcomes suggest that restrictions can carry political consequences and that support for legalization can endure after years of experience.

Georgia patients and consumers have been speaking up too. Please help secure a Senate sponsor, public hearings that include patients and homegrow advocates, and a vote on comprehensive reform.

Will you commit to championing legalization with homegrow included from the start? I would appreciate a written response explaining the specific reforms you will support and the steps you will take in the upcoming session.

Please show us that cannabis reform will become concrete action. Help us replace an illicit market with affordable, accountable choices and give Georgians the freedom to grow for themselves.

Respectfully

text:
Would You Let Trump Walk Away?

If Donald Trump agreed to leave power peacefully in 2028, would you let him spend the rest of his life playing golf in Florida?

That would mean no prison. No criminal trials. An easy and rich retirement for a man who has committed many crimes.

Countries have faced this dilemma throughout history: do you offer a leader who has done terrible things but still has power a safe retirement to get him to leave? Or do you threaten retribution and risk convincing him fight to the end?

Humans have a tendency to want revenge. To make people pay for their crimes. We want stolen money returned. We want justice.

We also want future presidents to understand that the government isn’t their personal piggy-bank, and that they can’t trample democracy and get away with it.

But consider the situation from the President’s side. If leaving the White House means going to jail and losing your fortune, clinging to power at all costs can become very attractive. Exit panic can lead to a scorched-earth exit.

Leaders who have abused their power have good reason to fear what happens when they leave. Saddam Hussein was captured, tried, and executed. Qaddafi was captured and killed. Leaders worry that they will pay a high price for stepping down.

To avoid that fate, leaders sometimes go to terrible lengths to stay in power: start a war, jail their opponents, or manufacture domestic unrest as an excuse to declare martial law. A crisis can give them a way to rally support or allow them to claim emergency powers to prevent being removed.

This is exactly what Israel has experienced since 2019 - the year Israel’s Attorney General brought corruption charges against Prime Minister Netanyahu, threatening to send him to prison. Suddenly, Netanyahu faced an existential crisis. If he stayed Prime Minister he could use all his power to avoid jail, but if he left he’d be much more vulnerable. One of the ways he maintained power, according to a New York Times investigation, was to prolong the war in Gaza (as well as start another war against Iran). It worked, for a while, but boy have Palestinians, Israelis, and Iranians paid a heavy price.

Do you see the dilemma? The threat of punishment can make a leader harder to remove. We don’t want presidents to think that their only way to stay out of prison is to stay in the White House.

History offers one way out: a safe, comfortable retirement. Think of it as a golden exit ramp. Ferdinand Marcos fled the Philippines and settled in Hawaii. Jean-Claude Duvalier spent nearly 25 years in exile in the south of France. Their citizens didn’t get the justice they deserved. But neither man ever ruled again.

Is this fair? Absolutely not. But is it better than a prolonged fight? In some cases, yes.

For Trump, the golden exit ramp would likely mean protection from prison and protection for his wealth. He could go back to Mar-a-Lago richer than he has ever been.

But that bargain carries a danger. The next wannabe kleptocrat could conclude that he, too, can plunder America and retire rich. Reward bad behavior and you risk getting more of it.

So what would a safer bargain look like? Trump would get to keep the substantial immunity he has already been given by the Supreme Court. And he would get to keep his money. But we would make sure that future presidents don’t get the same protection.

That would mean a constitutional amendment that ends presidential criminal immunity for future conduct. We should also require presidents to sell their businesses and publish their tax returns. Make it harder to profit from the presidency and give investigators the power to enforce those rules.

I know many of my readers will hate this idea. I hate it too. But history gives us reasons to consider it - clear cases where hated dictators really did disappear into golden retirements. Forever.

And think of the added benefit. The newly empowered Democrats could then focus on lowering gas prices, improving affordability, making it easier for people to buy houses, rather than fighting Trump and continuing to give him a stage.

In the end, this is what will win them votes in 2028 and make America’s future better.

text:
Expanded summary of the post
The November 18, 2026 post by @regulateRNM (VideoSAR / Jared Downer) is an open appeal primarily directed at @POTUS and secondarily at agencies and institutions including CDC, NIH, WHO, DARPA, NASA, MIT, Stanford, Harvard, IEEE, Thermo Fisher, and others. The core claim is that the author possesses a cure for cancer, which he describes as a fungal infection caused by melanized Candida. He attributes to this organism a wide range of additional capabilities:
•Oxidative stress protection
•Function as a natural, regenerating biosemiconductor via melanin-mediated electron transfer (MMET)
•Support for RF-based ocular heads-up displays
•hTERT-related age reversal and reduction of biological age (PhenoAge)
•Genetic modulation capable of addressing “every genetic disease”
•Compatibility with remote non-invasive deep brain stimulation (described as AI-BCI-DEW) and other radiofrequency or sonogenetic interventions
The post assigns extreme economic value to the discovery ($3–5 quadrillion for the core technology, $10 quadrillion+ over 70 years for related AI-BCI applications). It links this to funding mechanisms for worldwide universal basic income ($3–5k per month per country) plus security and vocational/retirement supplements. Additional claims include the existence of a frequency-based “kill switch” and a “dead man’s switch” that activates when the organism leaves range of “smart grid metal,” as well as compatibility with DARPA concepts such as a digital afterlife. The author offers partial ownership stakes (e.g., 1% of the melanization process to NASA if assistance is provided soon) and urges readers to “ask AI about a blacklight and synthetic melanin exposure.” The post ends by inviting further review (“Please see here:”) but does not include supporting data, methods, peer-reviewed references, or clinical results in the visible text.
Scientific context and status of the claims
Certain underlying phenomena are real and studied:
•Some Candida species (including C. auris) and other fungi can produce melanin, often as a virulence or protective factor. Melanin provides oxidative-stress resistance and has documented redox and electron-transfer properties. Research has shown that ionizing radiation can alter melanin’s electronic properties and, under certain conditions, enhance growth of melanized fungi.
•Extracted fungal melanins have been investigated in laboratory settings for anticancer effects (apoptosis induction, ROS modulation, photothermal applications), though these are experimental and far from clinical use as a systemic therapy.
•Fields such as sonogenetics, radiofrequency modulation of biology, biosensors, and telomerase (hTERT) research exist independently.

text:
HPSP & VA Scholarships for Medical Residency in the USA!

There are two major pathways worth understanding: Military HPSP/FAP and the VA Health Professional Scholarship Program (VA HPSP).

1. Military HPSP (Health Professions Scholarship Program)

Offered by:

U.S. Army

U.S. Navy

U.S. Air Force

Benefits:

Full medical school tuition coverage.

Monthly living stipend.

Certain additional financial benefits.

Access to military residency and fellowship training.

Important: Traditional military HPSP primarily funds medical school, not civilian residency. However, the military offers additional financial assistance programs for physicians in residency.

2. Military Financial Assistance Program (FAP)

Designed for physicians already accepted into eligible civilian residency programs.

Benefits include:

Annual grant (Navy: $45,000).

Monthly stipend.

Certain educational expenses.

Requirements:

U.S. citizenship.

Acceptance into an eligible residency.

Military officer eligibility.

Service commitment after training.

Source: [Navy HPSP & FAP]

3. VA Health Professional Scholarship Program (VA HPSP)

Offered by the U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs.

Benefits:

Full tuition at qualifying U.S. institutions.

Monthly living stipend.

Annual book stipend.

Employment opportunity with VA after graduation and licensing.

Eligibility:

U.S. citizenship.

Enrollment in an eligible, accredited U.S. medical education program.

Minimum 3.5 cumulative GPA.

Agreement to fulfill a VA service obligation.

Important for residency applicants:

Physician recipients must match into a residency as part of the program requirements.

Approved residency training may be deferred before fulfilling the VA service obligation.

Service obligations can extend up to six years, depending on the applicable program and agreement.

Source: [VA HPSP Official Website]

President salutes Zimbabwe's sporting champions

President Dr @edmnangagwa has saluted Zimbabwe's sporting champions, praising teenage gold medallist Ropafadzo Liberty Mzondo, the Warriors and the Sables for raising the nation's flag high and showcasing the immense talent, resilience and determination of Zimbabweans.

Speaking at State House during a reception held in honour of the country's recent sporting successes, President Mnangagwa congratulated 17-year-old Mzondo for winning Youth Olympic gold, describing the achievement as a historic milestone in Zimbabwean sport.

"Ropafadzo, you have demonstrated that success is not determined by age, background or circumstance, but by discipline, focus, hard work and courage," said President Mnangagwa.

The President also applauded the Warriors for their victory over Equatorial Guinea, saying the team's performance reflected teamwork, discipline and the indomitable Zimbabwean spirit.

While celebrating the achievement, he urged the national football team to remain focused on securing qualification for the Africa Cup of Nations (AFCON).

"The journey is not yet complete. The dream of returning Zimbabwe to continental football's grand stage remains firmly in your hands," he said.

President Mnangagwa paid tribute to supporters who braved rainy conditions to cheer on the Warriors, describing them as the nation's "12th man". He noted that Zimbabweans had long yearned for the return of international football on home soil, adding that the reopening of the National Sports Stadium, popularly known as Mugomba, has boosted the country's sporting momentum.

The Head of State also hailed the Sables for their hard-fought victory over Namibia, saying the achievements recorded by Zimbabwe's athletes and national teams belong to the whole nation and should inspire future generations.

Addressing young people, President Mnangagwa urged them to continue striving for excellence and flying the Zimbabwean flag high on regional and international platforms.

He reaffirmed Government's commitment to strengthening systems that identify, nurture and develop sporting talent from schools and institutions of higher learning through to the international stage, stressing that no one and no place will be left behind.

President Mnangagwa also assured the Warriors, their technical team led by coach Ramon Catala and all Zimbabwean athletes of the nation's unwavering support as they continue to bring pride and glory to the country.
